When the lady saw the rabbit, she was so surprised. "This is not a winged rabbit! This is a spirit called Wolpertinger!"
The hunter became more concerned. "Then what should I feed it?"
The elder lady searched her old memories, and answered. "I heard Wolpertingers eat wild berries and dews."
So the hunter began to collect berries every time he went out.

The hunter's wife made a cozy bed for the spirit, and the daughter went out to collect dewdrops early in the morning everyday. The family took care of the Wolpertinger with all their heart.
A season went by, and finally the Wolpertinger recovered its health. It was time for the spirit to go home. The hunter and his family went to the place where he first found the spirit. The little spirit flapped its wings but seemed hesitant to leave the family. Everyone was sorry to leave each other.
"Goodbye, fur ball. Don't get hurt again!" The hunter tossed the little spirit upward so that it could settle on one of the tall trees.
Soon after, the family heard strange voices!
"Thank you for helping out our little friend, ting!" "Good tall-tingers! You have Wolpertingers blessings, ting!" There were large Wolpertingers sitting on tree branches, looking down at the family. It was such an astonishing moment.
Since then, whenever the hunter went out, he always found plenty of games and fruits. Their family never went hungry again.

Dear Selena.

It's been a while. I hope you're doing well.
I did perform the research you requested in the Forest of the Great Tree.

The Great Sage Tree used to be the place of exchange between Elves and Humans, and it was preserved in a good condition. But this was also the place where wizards of dark magic killed many Elves. Elves must have been devastated by their attacks to leave such a beautiful place like this. Since Elves were gone, Ogres came in and took the place.

It was hard to find our actual research subjects, Wolpertingers. I had to wait for a pretty long time to see if the rumor in the village was true. But it was well worth it. When I waited long enough, Wolpertingers came one by one, and started to sing and perform a ritual.
So now I confirm the "rumor in the village" - the ritual of Wolpertingers, was indeed real. This was never recorded in any of the history books we have.

When the largest Wolpertinger sang, magical flowers bloomed around The Great Sage Tree, and shimmering will o' the wisps emerged from the flowers. Wolpertingers claim that they are Elven Souls that are shackled to this land. Wolpertingers call this ritual of sending away bound Elven Souls, the "Passage Ceremony."

But during the ritual, Ogres came out from the forest to steal Elven Souls. I stopped them with the help of other adventurers in the area. We just can't just let Ogres constantly disturb this important ceremony.

How about the Lightbringer Society help this ritual to go on, within the scope of not disturbing Wolpertingers? Maybe we could provide guidance to other adventurers, or write papers on this subject to make the public aware.
Let's discuss this when I go back to the Society.

- Adriel

My dear Martinay.

Hello, it's been a while. You must have been worried sick about me, I'm so sorry.

Oh, Martinay, I have a news for you. And that is... I do not suffer from mana frenzy anymore! I finally got full control of my magic! Can you believe it?

Ten years ago, when Arkeum spies tried to hurt you, a storm began to whirl inside me. Since then, the storm came and went. I felt like I was being cursed, whenever my magic went crazy.

But now I'm here, and I've been through so much. Now I'm strong enough to control the storm inside me. Well, I couldn't do this by myself. Have you heard of Janice? She helped me. I met her at the lighthouse, and later I found out that she was a renowned Archwizard. I was so lucky to meet her.

She helped me to find my peace, and to become one with the magic. I realized that understanding and accepting myself was the key to control my magic.

I have so much to tell you, but I can't go back to you for now. I have something to take care of. I can't tell you the details, but a terrible power that killed so many people long ago is about to come back, and I'm going to stop it.

I talked to Janice, and realized that it can be only stopped by people like me, other Star-Born. So that's what I'm going to do.

Martinay, I'll write you again soon. Thank you for all the love and support.

Ogres may seem uncultured and without intelligence, but they have their own traditions. Some tribes run secret rituals, and one of them is called the "Dance of Mating."

When the wind blows south and red trees are filled with sap, Ogres wait for the full moon and gather at a secret place. Then they build a tower with logs they brought in.
When the tower is complete, the ritual leader hits the tower with a hammer made of flintstone to lit a fire and roars to signal everyone to begin the ritual.
Male Ogres then start a peculiar group dance. They all move exactly the same way, even if no one taught them how to dance. The dance goes on until they become exhausted and pass out.
Female Ogres enjoy snacks or drum on trees as if playing a musical instrument while watching them dancing.
Only those who dance until the end can find their mates. We do not know how such ritual began, as they do not have a proper language to explain it to us, but we do believe this ritual must be their instinctive behavior to produce healthy offsprings.

Sept. 13th
I had to work early in the morning again. I was the night watch yesterday, so I dozed off, and Cervic, my senior, yelled at me. He said I should stay sharp if we were to deliver bitumen on time. But when do I get my sleep?

Sept. 14th
I went to work in the early morning again. Then I dozed off while carrying a bitumen bottle, and dropped it. No one saw me, so I covered them with dirt.

Cervic quietly asked me if I knew something about the missing bottle. I tried to deny it, but he said he heard me sleep talking. So I told him the truth. Cervic was afraid that they might crush his balls for this, and said he'd keep it secret. All's good that ends good, right?

Sept. 17th
My fingers have been itching since yesterday. When Cervic saw me scratching my fingers under the gloves, he came and asked me if I touched bitumen when I dropped it. I didn't sleep yesterday. I couldn't. The bitumen mutates you, if you touch it? Why didn't anyone tell me this before? Could it be true? So far, nothing happened but some itching fingers. My fingers are burning. I took off my gloves, and saw my fingers turned black. There were weird horn-like things between the fingers, too. I quickly put on the gloves again. Will they use me as a test subject? Or maybe they will cure me. Or not. What do I do? Should I run? Oh, man. I am so lost...

Rain was pouring on the day Master Lirel brought the young Ogre. The young boy was shivering, hiding behind my master... No one knew what kind of monster he was going to be back then.

Master Lirel was a proud Elven wizard, and he always took care of war orphans, regardless of their races. He taught orphans how to read and cast magic, saying every race deserved respect Master named the red Ogre "Khanzaizin."

Other children called him a dumb monster when master was not looking.

But I couldn't stand it anymore. One day, I knocked out one of the kids who were harassing Khanzaizin. Soon other kids overwhelmed me and beat the crap out of me, but still, it felt good.

When Master Lirel came back, he scolded all of us. Then after a long contemplation, he cast a magic on Khanzaizin.

Since then, Khanzaizin became smart enough to learn the human language. He looked up on me like an older brother since I saved him from bullies, and I taught him writings and magic spells.

I even gave him my favorite wand when I left to train swordsmanship. He was thrice bigger than me, yet seemed so sad.

After ten years of training, I became one of the elite magic swordsmen. And that was the year the war between Elves and Humans started. When I refused to kill Elves, they imprisoned me in the underground dungeon for disobedience. Then my commander came to find me after a few days.

He said a monster has been slaughtering our soldiers, and he'd let me go if I kill the monster.

So I left with my men to Talandre, where the monster was. When we entered a narrow path in a foggy forest, large shadows came out.

The attack was brutal. My men died with screams. I tried to fight, but something hit me and I fell. I think I heard a voice as I lose my consciousness.

"You... killed. Humans. Master Lirel. Human...! I will kill you all. You are a human, too. If you come back... I will kill you!"

When I woke up, I was among my dead men. One of them had a wand stabbed in his heart. It was the magic wand that I gave to Khanzaizin long ago.

Some people say scholarly advancement comes from constant study, but sometimes, a mistake presents a breakthrough. The bitumen purification device is one of them.

For the last few years, I've been studying the red fog at the Swamp of Silence to find a way to purify the corruption. Red Bitumen, a red fog concentration, was the key to the purification. Many scholars came to help, but we couldn't create any meaningful result.

Then, we decided to purify the contamination using heat, and created a bitumen purification device. We used flammable magical materials as a heat source, but it was not hot enough to purify bitumen.

We added coals to raise the temperature, but it didn't work.

When everyone was frustrated, one of the young researchers screamed. When we ran to see what happened, the researcher was sitting on the ground, with his both hands on his head. He accidentally added bitumen, instead of coals.

Then, something amazing happened. Magical materials reacted to bitumen, causing tremendous heat. We added more bitumen, and it worked. The heat radiated from the mixture successfully purified a small amount of bitumen. A contamination purifying itself!

From this experience, I realized that we should pay attention to everything when you run studies, even if it was an accident.

Swamp Sharks and Frogs (1)

Written by Flin Dextern

The "Swamp of Silence" is a desolate place where the disaster from thousands of years ago had struck. But contrary to its name, the swamp is literally filled with a multitude of lively sharks.
Sharks are usually found at sea, but these swamp sharks jump around the mud with their fins, almost like toads or frogs.
One of the researchers (he preferred to remain anonymous) who has been studying this place for a long time, explained the current status of the swamp like this:

"There have been so many theories regarding the evolutions of these creatures. But anything that says 'adaptation' is all garbage."

He said that research regarding the topic failed because these theories were founded on a wrongful assumption.

"The one common thing between frogs and sharks in this area are their high fertility rate."

He claimed that these changes were not an adaptation, but random events that happened during generations of propagation. He used Explosive Marsharks as an example.

"If there really is an evolution that is favorable to a creature itself, why would this shark evolve into a suicidal machine? This is proof that evolution is just a result of coincidence."

But he agreed that the contamination in this area is accelerating the creatures' mutations. And these endless mutations could help creatures to survive in the harsh environment.

"That's why I'm against purifying this swamp."

He was very careful when he said this to me. He seemed worried that other researchers might hear him.

"This place is like a laboratory that the gods have given us. Where would we ever find so many mutated creatures? Purifying this place will be a great loss for the biologists who study mutations and evolutions."

But many scholars are doing their best to purify this place, especially the Red Bitumen. Scholars believe that the Red Bitumen is the major source of contamination and mutations, as they are found in the sharks and frogs in the swamp as well. But the purification is delayed because not many adventurers visit this area due to the contamination.
"Are there other researchers who agree with you?" When I asked, he shuddered.

"Anyone who disagrees with the purification will be accused of being a Shadowmancer. But a scholar shouldn't be afraid of failure. Using this as an opportunity to learn something new is the only right thing to do as a scholar, don't you think?"

But then we had to stop the conversation because the other scholars came to us.
Whenever I visit this place, I think of this scholar. Humans are part of the nature. But how can you judge our actions as 'unnatural' or 'natural'? Maybe there is something in this topic that we have to think about.

A few years ago, a giant whale was found at the Swamp of Silence. People called it "Minutrite" because of its resemblance to Gigantrite, only smaller. Minutrite must have been buried under the mud for a long time, as it was covered with trees which made the creature almost like a little hill.

When I got to the swamp, Minutrite was lying still, breathing heavily. I was in awe when I saw this magnificent creature, and at the same time, my curiosity grew. My researcher friends and I climbed the creature to start our study. This creature was not as big as Gigantrite, but was almost the size of a small isle. The plants and rocks that grew out of its skin appeared to be contaminated. We were worried if this divine creature might not recover.

A renowned zoologist, Marius, theorized that this creature was of the same species as Gigantrite that we saw flying between Laslan and Stonegard, but about one thousand and five hundred years younger. There once was a saying that "every ship is born in Rokard."

It is said that Rokard Shipyard used to be at the northwest of the Rusty Anchor Coast. This place has turned into an accursed desolate swamp now, but it once was a busy place filled with ship crafting masters.

The shipyard was famous for high quality ships made by very skilled craftsmen. But suddenly, the red fog and tidal waves swept out the shipyard. The shipyard was never restored, and survivors left. The water level constantly went down, and eventually, the coast turned into a swamp.

Now the Rusty Anchor Coast is a graveyard for ships, filled with remains of bygone ships. You won't even find a single piece of the shipyard that once was the best facility in the world.

I felt even deeper remorse when I read the "Royal Rokard" article from the Solisium Encyclopedia page 327, line 5:

"The Royal Rokard was the masterpiece that put both the magic and science together; this ship will provide you the most magical experience."

The ship was never completed due to the red fog, though. I searched the Rusty Anchor Coast ruin to find any remains of the Royal Rokard, but I couldn't find this particular ship among the piled up wreckage. I could feel the passion of the craftsmen of the past from the wreckage, though. Now mark my words; I will finish the Royal Rokard, the dream ship that was never delivered, someday.
Karchars and Leviathan are apex predators. But their origins are not very well known.

They are an ancient species, about one thousand years old. Their vision has degraded, but their hearing and olfactory system are extraordinary. These two species look similar, so scholars believed that they originated from the same family.

But documents from the Temple of Truth tell different story. Leviathan made its first appearance when the red fog first came, and at the time Leviathan didn't look very different compared to now. On the other hand, Karchars were quite different back then, and evolved into their current form.

When considering the average speed of evolution, it would be safe to assume that Leviathan was already its current form, even before the red fog came.

It means Leviathan was already exposed to a certain element before the earthquake and finished evolving into its current form, and it is possible that this element was the primary source of the red fog.

This theory also could explain why Leviathan is much faster than Karchars, and can create red fog-like aura to influence nearby creatures.

The source element of the red fog will be my next research topic.

- Shark researcher, Aria Kresswell.

I started my research on Vampires twenty years ago. I used to be a healer, a shaman, and an undertaker. As an undertaker, my job was to restore seriously damaged bodies for their funerals, and the pay was pretty good. Then one day, when I was preparing a dead man for his funeral, something shocking happened. The dead man suddenly opened his eyes and sat up. I got so scared and called my wizard friend Rupert. The "dead" man came back to his senses when Rupert used healing magic on him, and explained to us what had happened. And his story changed my life forever.

The man's name was Sergio. He used to be a good sailor, but as he got older, it became harder for him to find a job. He spent his time drinking at bars, then one day, a mysterious nobleman came to him. The nobleman said he would give Sergio a fortune if he brought an empty ship to the southern sea of Talandre to this dock on the day of dark moon. Sergio was only too happy to accept the offer, and recruited other crewmen. He and his crewmen assumed the nobleman wanted the ship to carry some valuable treasure, and decided to steal some of the treasure for themselves.

After a few days later, on the day of the dark moon, a huge merchant ship emerged from a thick fog, just like the nobleman said. The sailors took hold of the ship and changed its course to the destined pier. Meanwhile, some of the crew along with Sergio went down to the cargo hold to find hidden treasures. The cargo hold was cold and creepy. When they lit a lamp, hundreds of coffins appeared. Terrified sailors ran to the deck, but Sergio was certain that treasures were hidden in the coffins. But when he pried open the lid of a coffin, he regretted his decision. Hundreds of vampires were sleeping in these coffins. The vampires opened their eyes, and feasted upon the poor sailors. The only survivor was Sergio.

Sergio blacked out when the leader of Vampires bit him, and woke up to sail the ship to the destination as he was ordered to. When the ship entered the port, the vampires turned into bats and flew away. The leader told Sergio to wait until his master came back, and left. When Sergio finished telling us the story, he begged us to free him from his monstrous master. But Rupert told Sergio that half-vampires couldn't be saved, even with magic. When he heard Rupert, Sergio threw himself under the sunlight right in front of our eyes in despair, and turned into ashes. Since that tragic experience, Rupert and I started researching a cure. After years of study, we finally created potions and magic spells that could stop half-vampires from fully turning into Vampires. We named them "Sergio Cure."
I wonder where all the Vampires on the ship have gone to?

In memory of Pirate King Adelico who was victorious at Rusty Anchor Coast

The ten year old girl had thorns on her arm.

This morning, I was on a shipwreck at the Rusty Anchor Coast to test my bitumen purification device. But then I heard a creaking sound, so I went out to see what was happening and found a girl looking for something to eat.

She was about ten years old, and had thorns growing out of her arms. The thorns looked very similar to the ones you see on plants; the size of thorns varied from an inch to the length of a palm. They seemed to have started growing at different times.

They were growing out from her skin, it must have been very painful for the girl.

It was a symptom I haven't seen before, but I assumed it was a mutation caused by the red fog. I wanted to see if I could help her, so I talked to her. But when she saw me, she ran.

When I came back to the camp, I found out that she was the one that people called "a Little Monster at Swamp Cave." If she really is the girl who's been surviving out there for years, she will be the key to the red fog purification process, because people usually don't last more than a year when they are exposed to the fog. I need more information on the girl.

Jan. 9th - Warm
I return after burying my daughter. Poor Giselle. She's crying out that she's hungry, ignorant of the fact that her mother is dead. You think I can't take care of you? Baby girl, I'll take care of you no matter what.

Mar. 11th - Cloudy
I came back from the swamp after finding food, all while carrying my granddaughter on my back. But I see thorns on the baby's arm. Is it because my eyesight is getting worse? I must be seeing things.

May 21st
This is all my fault. The thorn on the baby's arm keeps growing. The villagers who saw it are trying to kick us out, saying that Giselle has been afflicted with the Red Fog Curse. Why would they think Giselle is cursed? They deserve to be struck by lightning!

Dec. 4th - Cold
No one is willing to accept us. I went to the cave in the swamp with my granddaughter. At least we can keep ourselves protected from the freezing wind.

June 17th
Giselle couldn't sleep a wink and cried all night long. I haven't seen her in this much pain before. The thorn on the arm became as large as her finger. I can't imagine how much it hurts.

June 20th
I found a strange berry bush deeper in the cave while searching for herbs. I felt bad for giving her such bitter food, so I gave her a few berries. She regained her color and recovered quickly. I can't believe the remedy Giselle needed was so close by... Thank you, Einar!

Feb. 25th - Sunlight
It's been three years since we moved into the cave. I can't feed Giselle much, so she's small and bony. She's slow to speak as well. I wanted to play the role of her mother properly... I don't know how I'll face my late daughter.

April 8th
I slipped and hurt my back. Due to my age, recovery seems slow. I had no choice but to lie down and rest, but I'm worried about Giselle. What if she gets sick when we're out of berries...? A sigh slipped out at one point, and Giselle said, "No hurt, Grandma" while massaging my arms with her tiny hands. My sweet granddaughter...

April 10th
Giselle is in pain again because I couldn't feed her berries for a few days. It breaks my heart that the thing on her arm is tormenting her so. There's a lump in my throat from watching her shoulders tremble in pain. I'll get those berries tomorrow, at all costs.

April 11th - Sunrise
I managed to get some berries, despite my ailing body's best efforts. Giselle's condition improved almost instantly. She's finally smiling again. But, how much more time do I have to stay by her side...? This won't do. I must show her how to gather berries, and survive on her own

I have big plans for today. I promised to cook a Shrimp Sandwich for Giselle. Shrimp Sandwiches have been popular in Herba as of late for their taste as well as their high protein.

Giselle's been taking her medicine properly, and when I'm busy with my research she keeps to herself and quietly waits for me to finish. When I see her bright smile, all the exhaustion from my research just evaporates. I want to thank her by taking the time to cook her a proper meal. But, since I'm still not very good at cooking, my colleague Aindel offered to help me out.

The problem was catching the highlight of the dish: the Mantis Shrimp. I've heard you can catch them in the seas beyond the swamp, but I'm an even more experienced fisherman than I am a cook. Still, I foolishly wondered "how hard could it be?" and decided to try.

The sea was quiet. In that complete silence, without any sound from wind nor wave, I cast my lure.

It turns out, fishing is as boring and uneventful as it looks. I'm not an impatient man but after ages of waiting, I hadn't seen a single fish. Even Giselle, who was at first excited to tag along, quickly became bored after catching a few minnows darting in the shallows. She ended up taking a nap on a sunny rock.

I steeled my resolve again after seeing Giselle's face, and cast my fishing pole once again. At that moment, I felt a distinctive tug on my line. I assumed I'd imagined it, so I reeled back in slowly, not expecting to find anything. As I brought my hook out of the water, staring back at me, was a massive Mantis Shrimp. I couldn't believe it. I woke up Giselle immediately and she screamed with glee. "Azra, got fish!" she yelled as she ran around the shore. Her joyful laughter accompanied by the sound of the waves is a song I won't soon forget.

After celebrating for a short while, we started our journey back. Surely with a Mantis Shrimp this big and juicy, I can make her an exceptional treat.

Azra!

When Minutrite recovers and rises to the sky once again, you can get on its back at Swimming Hills to gather fresh Fan Leaves.

Then, all you need is vegetable oil, which you can get from Sundries Merchants.

Here's Chef Jaimy Ramzy's recipe. Read it carefully and follow it exactly.

I hope Giselle likes it!

Good luck,

Four Black Anvil Dwarven Hangover Solutions

Written by Jan Moerph

Everyone who's suffered a hangover would look for a good sobering up solution.
So I have experimented on four of the most popular hangover cures and compiled them into a report.
I hope this helps those who are suffering from a hangover.
Please note that the following is in chronological order, not their effectiveness.

1. Drinking Drake Blood
Drake blood starts to coagulate as soon as the creature dies, so it's very hard to get pure and clean Drake blood. Many drinkers believe that drinking pure and clean Drake blood before you consume alcohol prevents you from getting drunk. But when I tried it while I was drunk, it didn't work. I was still drunk, and had a serious headache. Then after an hour, I ran to the bathroom to empty my body both ways, and my hangover got slightly better. Drinking the blood prior to consuming alcohol might work, but if you drink it afterwards, expect some discomforts.

2. Breathing in Talandre Gale
There is a saying that breathing in gales of Talandre improves one's blood circulation. That's probably why you see so many drunkards climb the mountain and keep their mouths open to let the wind in. Well, the cold strong wind does help you to sober up. But, be careful not to slip when you climb. My back still hurts from my last fall.

3. Holding an Obsidian in Your Mouth
Some people put a little piece of Obsidian in their mouths when they are drunk. They claim that Obsidian absorbs alcohol, but when I tried it, I just cut my palate. The pain kind of sobered me up, but I'm not sure if I should call it an "effective hangover cure."

4. Drinking Rock Water from the Mine

The reason why the mine is heavily guarded is because of this water. Bonia Naru only drinks water from this mine, and put soldiers to guard the water. This water filtered by Obsidian is said to be clean and has a lot of healthy elements, and cooled rock water improves your health and cures hangovers. I finally had a chance to try this water, when I won a bet with one of the water guards. It tasted like ordinary water when I first drank it, but on the next day, it was as if I never drank any alcohol in the first place! I felt so healthy and fine. I went back to the water guard fellow to ask him about the water, but he was not there, and I never saw him again. Maybe he's in the prison for giving me the water. I would love to try the water again, but I don't think I will ever get the chance.

I also tried rubbing cold Obsidian on my body, but it didn't really work.
So far, the best hangover cure I found was drinking the rock water from the mine. But I will have to risk my neck to get the water, so that's a no-no. Rock water from other mines might work, but I don't want to search all the mines just to get some hangover cure.
So, here is my conclusion: the simplest solution for simple Dwarves like me.
Do you have a hangover? Then drink more! A hangover comes to you only when you stop drinking. So, keep drinking! Getting drunk every day is the best hangover cure and is the best way to live a happy life!

- Jan Moerph, the happiest Dwarf in the world

The Story of the Spineflower Knights

Written by Flin Dextern

Talandre used to be a natural fortress surrounded by high rocky mountains, but after the Breezeline Station opened at Herba Village, it became a tourist spot. In the village square, there is an old lady named Serine, and she has been there since I started frequenting Talandre as a young man. She knows a lot of old stories and histories of Talandre, and the one about the Spineflower Knights was one of the most interesting stories she has ever told me.

"A long time ago, Talandre was ruled by Duke Bercant. He had a daughter named Limuny, and she was the bravest and smartest person in the province."

Serine started her story.

"The duke also had a son, but he sent away the son to Arkeum because he was afraid that the boy might steal his fief. So Limuny became the actual protector of this land."

Limuny Bercant was a smart woman, and she was good with swords. She trained other ladies and founded an order of knights, the Spineflower Knights. For over ten years, the lady knights and their soldiers protected the land.

"Every family wanted to send their daughters to the Spineflower Knights. The knights were very well respected, and the pay was good, too."

But when the duke died, things became serious. Yonhark Bercant came back from Arkeum to inherit the land and his father's title, and the feud between siblings began.

"The greedy son had no intention to share the power with the lady. Can you imagine her frustrations? Limuny was the one who actually ran everything in this land."

Their relatives sided with Yonhark, only because the duke used to prefer his son over the daughter.
Then, a tragedy happened. No one knows why, but a terrible monster emerged from the basement of the Bercant Manor. Serine said that Limuny might have unleashed a curse or something out of fury.

Anyways, Limuny turned into a plant because of this florification curse, along with all the knights from the Spineflower Knights.
I was so curious to see humans turned into plants, so I started to head towards the Bercant Manor, but Serine stopped me.

"Don't go, young man. Do you know how dangerous it is over there? And florification is contagious!"

Serine said the florification affected not just the knights, but everyone around the manor. Families of the fallen knights and people who tried to run away. Everyone who was at the Bercant Manor were now monsters.
Serine didn't know where the curse came from, but said it was greed of the noble family who killed everyone.

"Always stay modest. Greed destroys you, even noblemen. You remember that!"

Such wise words from an old lady who must have lived more than a hundred years. But still, I want to see. Maybe I'll get some help from the Resistance to actually explore the horrible historic site.
Wounds caused by florified monsters have a high chance to turn victims into trees. Most of them die during the painful mutating process, but even if they survive, they turn into soulless monsters.

Florification is a plant related curse magic, based on a shamanic spell that druids in the forest used.

It was originally intended to be a healing spell; what they tried was to plant microspores in a human body, and let it fight against viruses that caused illnesses. But spores multiplied out of control unexpectedly, causing florification on patients.

Eventually, druids forbade the use of this magic, and soon it became forgotten. The person who revived florification in Solisium was Sylon, an assassin who worked for the Crimson Family.

Sylon used to be a druidic shaman, but when his tribe was massacred during the war, he turned to the Crimson Family to avenge his fallen kins. The Crimson Family was kidnapping countless people and performed various experiments on them to create the most lethal magic spell.

After ten years of research, Sylon finally created a very contagious and lethal magic using the forgotten florification curse along with dark magic. But right before the final test, an accident happened - test subjects caged in the Crimson Mansion basement escaped and killed everyone in the Crimson Mansion, including Sylon.

Florified monsters then moved on to attack people in the nearby villages. Time went by, and most of the test subjects and infected victims died, but it was not over yet. They sowed seeds, and some of their bodies were setting roots into the soil.

The ruined Bercant Manor features a dilapidated ranch. It's deserted now, but in the past it was filled with healthy sheep and numerous shepherds. Sam was one of those young shepherds.

Sam and the other shepherds' favorite time of the day was when the daily necessities arrived from the mansion. Of course they appreciated the snacks inside the basket, but they were mostly looking forward to seeing Norn Bercant, who came with the basket. Norn was the kindhearted and beautiful second daughter of the Bercant Family. Sometimes, she would carry the huge basket all by herself without bothering the servants to help her. She prided herself in doing chores around the ranch and helping out wherever she could. The shepherds loved her visits as she was a fantastic listener who put up with their endless chattering without getting irritated. But one day, Norn wasn't there to drop off the basket. This concerned some of the shepherds, including Sam, who went to look for her. When Sam finally spotted her leaving the manor, he followed her all the way into a twisted forest. In the forest, a handsome young man was waiting for Norn. Norn and the man looked around to see if they were alone and then held hands while they took a walk in the forest.

Sam concluded from their careful behavior that they obviously felt this relationship needed to be kept a secret. The shepherd boys felt for the young couple and swore as a group to keep Norn's secret.

But the young man they saw with her was named Lazarus and he was from the Crimson Family. Norn and Lazarus's relationship brought catastrophe to both families and many lost their lives. The shepherd boys and the neighbors were even swept up in the mess. Before this great tragedy struck, Sam left Talandre with his family. When he heard of the disaster, he regretted keeping their meeting a secret. But even if he had spoken up, no one would've listened to a mere shepherd boy, though that fact didn't give him any consolation. Until the moment he died, he regretted his decision. He so badly wanted to repent himself by visiting the Bercant family's grave. On behalf of Sam, who is no longer with us, I leave his story. Great-grandfather, please find peace in the heavens now.

The royal family of Solisium gifted fine horses to the Bercant Family in recognition of their achievements. After that family's fall, the surviving horses found new owners. But because these horses were so special, there are many interesting stories about them.

1. Solar Melody: Horse of Elegance

Solar Melody was a particularly emotional horse with a great ear for music. At the nearby sheep ranch, there was a shepherd boy who often played the flute. Whenever that boy played, Solar Melody would stop whatever it was doing and just listen to the music, despite the horsemen's' scoldings. The problem was that the boy played flute very often and at completely random times. Because the horse couldn't be trained or put to work due to the music, the head horseman finally found the shepherd boy and made a variety of threats about what would happen if he ever played that flute again. But clever Melody realized what had happened and came up with an innovative idea to rebel against the horsemen. Melody would not excrete until it could hear the sound of the flute. In the end the horsemen caved, realizing they were risking the health of a prized horse, and begged the shepherd boy to play again, but only at certain times. The shepherd boy, realizing what was going on, insisted that if he was to perform at scheduled times, he'd have to be paid like a scheduled performer. Which they reluctantly did.

2. Luminous and Ebony Ramtane: A Battle of Beauty

Just as there is a standard of beauty for people, there is one for horses. Luminous was a tall, slim courser with a beautiful golden coat. Ebony Ramtane was a dark horse with a pitch black coat. Its build was big and strong, making it seem ever so valiant. Because both horses were so aesthetically pleasing, many visitors lined up to see them. As such, the two horses traveled together often. They spent a lot of time together, and a strange sort of competition sprung up between the two prized horses.

Luminous had an outgoing personality, so it would often enjoy posing and accommodating the requests of the crowd for tricks. However, right when a painter would set up their easel to draw the magnificent horse, Ramtane would come along with his strong muscles put on a show, blocking Luminous. But Luminous was no better. When Ramtane was the center of attention, Luminous would stroll in and steal Ramtane's thunder. These two hypercompetitive horses always put on quite a show. Unfortunately, the two horses were adopted into different families, so the entertaining competition came to an end.

The dead bodies rose, and bit the man with their teeth. The man tried to fight back the dead bodies, looked at me, and pointed at the torch. I picked it up and threw it at the dead bodies.

This man was on a mission to find the escaped Immortus and burn them. The document said that anyone who was bitten by Immortus would come back to life and become one of them. On the next day, I heard a news that Edgar's body disappeared. Also, the number of mysterious monster attacks on people near the Crimsons' estate has increased ever since. I am an old woman now, old enough to know the ways of the world, but I still get chills when I think of that horrible day. I didn't dare ask the housekeeper why, but other maids told me weird stories; that monstrous sounds are heard from the basement at night and such. There was also a rumor that the Crimsons were not just ordinary hunters, but actually man hunters. They were horrible and fascinating stories, and maids loved to talk about them.

But then someone crossed the line. A very brave and nosy maid actually went to the basement to see if all the rumors were true. But then she got caught by Millar, and was fired right on the spot. Then dead people came back to life, and started to make another victims. I ran to Herba Village and survived, but what I saw on that day was burned into my mind.

I wish I didn't go to the village on that day. I am glad that I was not brave or nosy enough to go the basement. I'm glad it was not me who turned into the horrible monster...

This happened to me when I just started my career as a sculptor. At that time, I was a novice apprentice running errands under a very well known sculptor, Mark Stone. One day, he received a strange request from the Crimson family of Talandre. They wanted statues for the shrine of their ancestors.

Mutants of Plateau

Written by Flin Dextern

Talandre is known for high mountains and harsh environments. On the northern side of Talandre lies Mount Snowburn, where its perpetual snow creates a beautiful vista.
This mountain is very high and steep, so it's not easy for humans nor monsters to climb. It made the place a very well reserved natural habitats of rare wild animals and plants.
But while I was travelling the area, I heard a disturbing story that Plateau Goats and Plateau Peacocks that were native to this mountain were being attacked by mutants.

"It's been happening for a while now. Weird looking ones coming up, and attacking the native species."
Lumis, my mountain guide and a hunter explained the situation to me.

"Mutants are easy to spot. Especially peacocks. The native peacocks are white, which is their protective color, but mutants can be just whatever you can think of - red, blue, you name it."

I followed Lumis to peacock's habitat, and I could see them from afar. White ones at the top of the mountain were relatively easy to spot as it was already summer, but if I came here in winter, I wouldn't have been able to identify them easily. Mutant peacocks at the lower part of the mountain were even easier to spot due to their gaudy color. What creeped me out was their colors were just so out of place, just like monsters you see out there.

"When mutants run into each other, they fight to death. Even worse, these mutants taste bad. Some of them are even poisonous."

Lumis was worried that these aggressive mutants were killing the native peacocks.

Then I got curious, and asked him to show other mutants. So he led me to where Plateau Goats and their mutants were. Just like peacocks, the native Plateau Goats were living in the higher altitude, and mutants stayed in the lower places.

"You see that? These mutants have three eyes and four horns. And that their horns are just useless, look at their shapes."

Plateau Goats were famous for beautiful straight horns. But these mutants were hard to hunt, their horns were misshaped, and fur and leather were too stiff and bristly.
Lumis said these mutants came dozens years ago. I asked him why people didn't do anything about it, he answered.

"At the beginning, there weren't that many. We just thought they were going to go away."

He said the number of mutants multiplied recently. Lumis thought the Crimson Mansion was the reason behind all this, and the thing that caused mutation in the mansion must have somehow affected wild animals.
But the mansion was too dangerous to investigate, and the Resistance couldn't do anything but to watch them from outside.

"I am worried that our native Plateau Peacocks and Plateau Goats might go extinct. If they are gone, we would have nothing to hunt."

Lumis said maybe spreading this news might attract the attention of experts who might be able to work out this problem. I don't know if his idea would actually work, but anyone who's interested in this issue, please come to the Snowburn and help them to investigate further on the mutated goats and peacocks.

"S, I won't go back."

The hint was hidden in the first picture. As I stretched my hand for it, the sentence disappeared into the wind. To find him, I must go deeper, and further.

He was my lover. An explorer, a dreamer, always chasing his dreams. And this time, he was chasing treasure. He said that a priceless treasure was hidden in a painting. He left without hesitation and never returned.
I searched through all the records to find his traces. And in his room, I found an invitation with the name "Kailos" written on it.
That's how I arrived in this Hall of Illusion. There was a strange silence in the hallway. The paintings in the frames seemed to be silently watching me. I instinctively chose one painting that called to me and reached out with my hand. At that moment, my vision distorted and a golden sandstorm swept over me.
Three suns were floating overhead. The air was hot, and the sand beneath my feet rippled as if it were alive. Had he passed by here? I searched for clues in the desert where not even a single footprint remained. And then I found a sentence engraved with magic in the deepest part of the desert.
"S, I won't go back." It was the message he left behind. Is this the last trace of him? Is he alive? In which painting can I find him? But... What if he chose a new life here?
I was shaken. But before I knew it, I was back in the hallway, standing in front of another painting, this time glowing purple.
As I reached for it with my hand, a purple wave rippled through the painting.

I have fantasized about the unknown since I was a child. While other children played with toys, I would open old maps in my parents' study and imagine lost civilizations. Mythical relics, ornaments from distant continents, mysterious statues of unknown figures. They were not just objects, but contained stories of a world I did not know, and I wanted to be the master of those stories. Finding the forgotten relics of the world became my life's goal.
That day was no different. I entered an abandoned castle to find relics of a forgotten ancient kingdom. Dusty relics were sleeping in the deep underground chambers of the castle. However, the object I was looking for was not there, and instead, a painting caught my eye. It hung in a corner, lost in its light, but I was pulled to it with an inexplicable force.
Under the twilight sky expressed with rough brushstrokes, fog rose above the endless valley. In the fog, hazy figures appeared vaguely, and they seemed to be staring at me. It felt too vivid and strange to be a simple work of art.
The moment I instinctively reached out, the painting shook with purple waves. My body floated up with a sense of losing gravity, and the next moment, I was in an unfamiliar place.

The cold, damp air penetrated my skin. In the darkness, fog flowed slowly, and beyond it, unidentifiable shadows floated low. A low, long sound emanated from somewhere, enveloping the space. It was as if the space itself was breathing. At first, I couldn't tell what was happening. But soon I realized. I was in the world of the painting.
As I pushed through the fog, the shadows that had been floating low became clearer. They were not of this world. They were beings from an unfamiliar dimension. When they finally wrapped around my ankles and slowly crawled up, a cold air seeped into my bones. A suffocating tension came over me.
I had to get out. The moment I instinctively shrank, the purple magic inside me reacted. An intense light flashed and the space shook. I returned as if I had been thrown into the basement of a castle. I looked up at the painting again, gasping for breath. The valley was still covered in mist, and something was stirring in the darkness.
I then realized. This was not just a painting, but a door to another dimension. My heart raced. What I wanted was not just a relic. This was what I had been searching for, the key to a new world. I had to find more paintings.
I left the ruins with the painting in my arms. A new journey was beginning.

"No, the hill! They are up on the hill!"
"Then we'll go to both the spots! Soldiers, move to the rally point!"

The Arkeum commander snapped at confused soldiers. Then she came into the cave and talked to the soldiers who were guarding the Storage Keepers.

"I'll take the goblins now. I'm moving them to the safer location."
"Sir? But our order was..."
"Silence! Now, go out and hunt down the Resistance!"

Scared soldiers hurried out of the cave.

The commander approached the cage, and smashed the lock with a sword.

"Lati! Labo! It's me, Casena. We have to go!"

The commander took off the helm, and it really was Casena. She dropped the heavy armor, installed explosives around the cave, held the brothers' hands, and started to run.

"It's going to blow! Careful!"

Then everything exploded with a flash. The shock stumbled Casena, but she soon regained her composure and jumped on to the Magic Circle with goblin brothers. Their visions blurred, and they were back at their own camp in an instant. People cheered, while Casena's warm hands were still holding the brothers' hands.
When I saw the gigantic shape emerging from the darkness, I understood the fear that my grandfather had all his life.

Dear grandfather,

My hands are still shaking as I write you this letter, and my heart is burdened with a grave guilt.
I have revived Grimturg, the monster that you have feared all your life. And the monster has destroyed all the faith I had in me. When the emperor gave me the royal order, I was nervous. But my accursed curiosity has blinded me; I obediently followed the royal order, but in reality I did what I did only to satiate my selfish desire. I prepared the Magic Circle deep within the island and recited the spell, as if I was in a vague dream. It was exciting even, to see a huge portal opening up and gloomy energy creeping out from the hole. Finally, Grimturg emerged from the gate.

When I saw the gigantic shape emerging from the darkness, I understood the fear that my grandfather had all his life. I realized that I never understood your words truly, up until the moment.
Its menacing gaze was fixed on us, and hands reached for my students. There were torn flesh and blood everywhere, and I was just standing there in shock, doing nothing. That must be what you have felt when you met Grimturg. The monster massacred my students with its chain, casting death magic.
I couldn't do anything.

I had no courage to stand up in the middle of horrible massacre. It was as if my brain has shattered. I fled in unspeakable shame.
I have committed an unforgivable sin. I set a horror to roam free in this world.
How will I pay for this sin?
Now someone else will have to stop the monster that I summoned. This is my letter of penance for you, grandfather. I have ruined what you did for us.


Your grandchild who ruined everything, Alterion

This is a record of Cage's life and advice for the future generation.

Cage was born from a rich family, and had enjoyed opulent life. Then the boy grew up to be a gambler and an alcoholic, wasting away his family fortune. When he lost everything, he went to see his mother. But all he found was his already passed away mother's last letter. "My dear son, I'm sorry that I could not see you before I leave. I have nothing to give you but my necklace. Keep it close, it might protect you."

Cage shed some tear, but soon he decided to sell the necklace for another card game or two. But merchants were not interested in the necklace. So he tried to sell it on the street, but ran into his debtor and was beat up. Cage begged the man for more time, and the debtor offered him a choice.

"Go to Nebula Island and bring me treasure. If you succeed, your debt will be paid in full, and I will even reward you." There was no choice. Cage went to the island with other graverobbers. The sea breeze filled him with a new hope, that everything might work out fine.

But the island was different from his imagination. It was a place filled with monsters and death; his team was attacked by monsters, and he had to flee by himself. When he couldn't run anymore, he heard voices. Cage followed the voices to ask for help, but people he found were hunters who were there only for the treasure. They jumped on him, and Cage ran again. Then he lost consciousness in the middle of an Orc village.

When he woke up, an Orc shaman was looking down on him. Cage thought he was going to die, but the shaman pointed at his necklace.
"Where did you get the necklace?" Cage said it was from his father. The shaman grew curious, and told him a story.

Ten years ago, he found an injured human and helped him without telling his tribe. Then when his village was attacked by Arkeum Legion, the human came back and fought against Arkeum to help Orcs.

The Orcs finally won the battle, and the Orc village chief gave the human a necklace as a gift for his valor.
Cage realized that his father had a special tie with this Orc tribe. This necklace was not a simple accessory, but a symbol of friendship and trust. Cage's father saved the Orc shaman, and in turn, the shaman saved cage to leave the island safely.

This event changed Cage forever. He reflected on his shameful past, and swore to walk a new path.
While keeping the lesson his father has taught him close to his heart.
I shouldn't have opened the chest. It was filled with horror and destruction beyond my imagination.

It was only a happenstance that I found a chest today. The chest was unnaturally cold to my touch, which reminded me of every creepy rumor that I heard about chests with relics.

"People who touched the chest pass out right on the spot," "A man just looked at the chest, and killed himself after suffering from horrible nightmares," "A soldier who opened a chest went mad, and attacked his comrades." But no, these were only rumors. Rumors didn't scare me.

So I decided to open the chest. If there really was a relic inside, Kazar would have rewarded me well. But when I opened the chest, strange mana surrounded me and whispered into my ears.

"Thou who shall have the power... Come to me... Wake me..." I was terrified, but I tried to calm myself saying that it was a hallucination that my mind created.

Then a thick dark fog from the chest surrounded me. I saw a vision of a man with a blank look. As he approached me, my heart began to race.

Amidst the suffocating fear, I asked myself a question. What was Kazar looking for? What power did the relic had? Then I blacked out.

When I woke up, I was sitting at my own camp. My friends say that I was dreaming, but I know that is not the case. Because I still hear the voice.
Hanging bodies on the tree - that was the last of those who disobeyed Kazar.

When Kazar gave me his order, I knew everything was going to change. The soldiers who believed that it would be okay to steal a couple of treasure will have to change their minds.

As per Kazar's order, I wrapped the thieving soldiers with wet clothes from head to toe, and hung them on the tree. Soldiers wriggled and begged and cried like big white worms, but they all died away with thirst and starvation.

Others turned their heads away from the gruesome punishment. It filled them with fear and anxiousness. Kazar's message was clear. Whether relic we find is magical or not, anyone who touches them will pay.

It made me realize that Kazar was obsessed with relics, even to a lethal degree. I don't know the reasoning behind this, but the relic he is looking for must worth all these cruelty. I have also accepted the fact that I must be the part of this madness, as the executioner of his instructions.

My men know this, too. I feel their desperation, but I will never show my fear. Because I am just a tool, a tool that Kazar uses.
Rosaline, you and Allen are the only thing that keeps me going. If it weren't for you, I would have died already.

My beloved Rosaline,

How are you and Allen doing? I didn't expect to be sent off to this remote island, as soon as I joined the Arkeum Legion.
This place is horrible. The tent is suffocatingly narrow and moldy. My blanket is soggy and cold, but I still need them because it's so windy here. My ration is a disgusting gruel that makes me want to puke. Muddy puddle everywhere, and I fear that my feet would go rotten in these muddy shoes.
You and Allen's portraits are what keep me going. I forget pain and fear when I look at your portraits.
Oh man, the commander is summoning. I have to go. Please tell Allen that I love her. I hope to see you soon.

Your beloved husband.

My dear Rosaline,

It's been ten days since my last letter.
Everyday there's a battle. We're fighting the Resistance for relics, risking our lives. I was afraid at first, but I don't feel the fear any longer.
Something horrible happened a few days ago. I had to hang my friends who tried to steal the treasure on a tree. I wrapped them with white sheets while they were alive. The horror...! I feel like I'm losing touch.
Rosaline, I think I'm forgetting you and Allen's faces. I've been looking at your portraits a lot more so that I won't forget.
Oh, it's time for my shift. I want to tell you more, but I have to go. I hope my next letter goes better than this.

Your beloved husband.

My dear Rosaline,

I don't remember the last time I wrote you a letter. Endless battle and cruel punishments are ruining me. I think I went mad on the day I hang my friends.
You are all strangers to me. I don't remember your smile nor Allen's laughter. This dark place swallows everything. Me, us, and my memories.
I want to go back. Back to you and Allen. I want to sit at the dinner table with you, laughing and joking. But I'm a goner now. My soul is destroyed. Perhaps it would be the best for you that I stay here forever.
Please, forget about me, and move on to live a happier life with Allen.

Your husband, who will never go back.

Casena Recruitment Operation Report

We have been paying attention to certain personnel named Casena. She is not a soldier nor Resistance, but she is a de facto commander of the Resistance relic recovery operation. She is a talented individual, and is the "pillar" of the Resistance in this area. In other words, she is a threat.
If we do not neutralize her, her existence in long term might hinder our operation. However, her superior tactical insights and organization ability are something that we could use.

Preface. Where did Orcs in Nebula Island come from?

They sailed the shark ridden sea with small rafts.

Why did Nebulaka Orcs choose this dangerous island over Laslan?

Many scholars believe that these Orcs are descendants of the Kalturan Clan, which is now gone. This is called Kalturan migration theory.

Kalturan Orcs were famously known to live with wolves. They relied on wolves from hunting to gathering. If Nebulaka Orcs really were descendants of Kalturan, why do they have no wolves?

Now, this is where my theory comes in. I think there was an unknown third Orc clan in Laslan, beside Fonos and Kalturan. As they were too small to compete against Fonos and Kalturan, they sailed out to the sea, and became the only Orc clan on Nebula Island.

A bold and groundbreaking theory, but the Society insulted me and my thesis. All they cared about was Fonos and Akidu, and they wanted nothing to do with something new. Cowards. I couldn't bear these imbeciles insulting me.

So I went out to find a ticket to Nebula Island. I needed something substantial to verify my theory on Nebulaka Orcs. There was a Resistance ship sailing to Nebula Island, but they refused to let me aboard. They said the island was a lawless pandemonium filled with Arkeum Legion and ruthless treasure hunters. Their words did not scare me.

I finally found a boat with a sailor to take me to the island. The Resistance ship heading towards the island was our guide. Orcs must have sailed the sea just like me a long time ago, without any guidance.

A long time ago, Travis VI chose Nebula Island as a storage for his special bounties, and kept it as a secret. But when Arkeum Legion invaded the royal secret library, the island became known to the public.

1. Orcs on Nebula Island

Orcs must have hated it when the existence of their island became public. The once peaceful island became a battleground of relic hunters and Arkeum Legion.

Many Orc villages were destroyed because of the conflicts between Humans, and Orcs lost many good warriors during the process.

2. Humans on Nebula Island

Humans on the Nebula Island have no trust between each other. At one moment, Treasure hunters would unite and fight against Arkeums; then after the battle, they would try to slit each other's throat. Sometimes I pondered if it was the relic on this island that made people so evil. If that was the case, it was no wonder that Travis VI tried to hide his treasure. What's even more concerning is that the situation is worsening.

I'm seeing more hunters focusing on killing rather than finding the relic. These people are willing to hunt anyone on sight. They are intoxicated by utter chaos.

When I was taking a nap hiding in the bush, I heard the Chief Priest's voice. It was so close, it gave me a jolt awake. The Chief Priest was very strict, even to the youngsters like me. He already caught me taking a nap before, and I was afraid what was to befall me this time. I began to crawl away from the spot, thinking I might get away as he had bad eyesight. But, there was a human in black armor standing next to him. Humans had good eyes. I hid myself in the bush again.

The black armor man was from Arkeum Legion, and he said a human king buried precious treasure in our island a long time age. He also said that as the current human king is Arkeum, we should bring the treasure to them, if we ever found one. Otherwise they were going to kill us all!

When the human finished talking, the Chief Priest spat on the man. And said that he would fry them and eat them if they don't leave our village right now! The Chief Priest swung his staff, and a real lightning struck down! I almost screamed.

The lightning narrowly missed the human. The human aimed his sword at the Chief Priest. But the Chief Priest didn't even flinch, just giving him evil eyes. Strangely, the human just left without a word. Then the Chief Priest stumped to the village with an angry face. I waited until it was quiet, and crawled out of the bush.

Perhaps the big chest I saw outside the village was containing the said relic. Maybe I should talk to the Chief Priest. But he wouldn't like it if he learnt that I was taking a nap outside of the village. I finally decided to wait until the tribe meeting. But the Chief Priest never held the meeting for days. If there really was a precious relic on this island, surely the Chief Priest would have told us, right? Or... maybe he's already collecting the relic for his own good. Kraak, that's petty!

So I decided to stay close to the priest. He would give me more errands, but on the other hand, I would know if he acts strangely. If he's really collecting the relics for himself, I will catch him and make a deal with him - free nap tickets everyday!
Until now, I believed that Orcs were harmful. Killing them was a natural thing to do. But this little Orc changed me completely.

I still remember the moment an arrow dug into my leg. A black snake mark on the arrow indicated that it was shot by the Black Snake Guild. They were following us around, and ambushed us when we were weak. I was separated from my group, and couldn't go to the designated rally point because of the injury. I hid myself in a ruin, and lost consciousness.

When I woke up, I realized that I was in a very bad situation. The "ruin" I was in, was an abandoned building of Nebulaka Orcs. I tried to stand up, but the pain was too great and could not walk at all.

Then I heard light footsteps. I gritted my teeth and hid behind a cover. After a while, when I peeked, there was a young Orc staring at me. Then the youngling disappeared. I thought the boy was gone to bring grownups.

But when the boy came back, he had a bag of water and some fruits. I looked at him warily, and the boy offered me the food and drink, making a gesture to eat. The boy didn't seem to have any ill intentions, so I took the food. It was a complicated feeling, eating food from an Orc boy.

So, I was contemplating the situation all alone, and loud noises were heard from the outside of the building. It was Arkeum Legion attacking the village for relics. I thought it was my time to leave, but then I heard the boy's scream. So I decided to fight, even if it would cost me a leg.

Orcs seem surprised when they saw a human covered with blood and dirt coming out of an abandoned building, but when I started to fight against the Arkeum, they joined me. How reckless I was! But I knew that I would never regret this day.

It was a hot and humid day. I heard a cry so I followed the voice, and I found a little Orc caught in a hunter's net. The Orc child fought me fiercely when I got close, but when I set him free, the child calmed down. When I told the him that I would take him to the Nebulaka Clan, he told me the story of Ktar, the hero of Nebulaka Clan to return the favor.

***
The Nebulaka Clan hated humans. Humans raided their villages all the time. Orc warriors fought bravely, but Humans were too strong.

Their Chief Priest has finally stood up to protect their clan. He prayed to Flamakan, and the god answered them with the fiercest warrior that Orcs ever had.

"Flamakan has answered our prayers! Our blesses warrior Ktar will protect us, and avenge our weak who already passed away!"

Ktar was the strongest and biggest Orc, and everyone cheered for him. Even Humans started to avoid this monstrous Orc. Some of them tried to fight Ktar, but all ended up dead or met fate worse than death. Finally, Humans completely gave up on raiding Nebulakan Orcs. Peace was here, finally... or so Orcs thought.

After Humans were all gone, Ktar got bored and began to harass Orcs, smashing and throwing things. Children ran at the sight of Ktar, and old Orcs stayed at home to avoid him. Ktar constantly picked a fight on other Orcs, and yelled at them when Orcs criticized him.

"I am so bored! I need to fight! Fight me!"

When the damage became too great, Orcs began to discuss for solutions, but there wasn't really anything they could do. One of the elder Orcs asked.

"If his problem is boredom, why don't we play with him?"
"Ktar is too wild, we cannot play with him."
Then, one of the Orcs came up with an idea. He collected Cracker Frog eggs and pour them on Ktar's clothing. Every time Ktar moved, eggs popped with weird farting sound. Ktar was upset, but he didn't have the time to beat up the culprit because he was too busy to clean up his clothes.

Orcs, watching this, gravely nodded and went out to find other tools of revenge... I mean, "toys." For example, an Orc brought Red Spot bees with gigantic wings and released them whenever Ktar tried to sleep to wake him up with buzzing sound.

Since then, Ktar never had a dull moment with all these tortures... I mean, "jokes." He went into hiding, refusing to meet anyone. He even missed his meals.

An elderly Orc took pity on him, and brought him fish and fruits everyday. It moved Ktar, and he apologized the elderly for his bad behavior. This elderly Orc was one of the wisest and skillful one, but he never showed off. Ktar learned a lot from his modest attitude, and it changed him - into the true hero of Nebulaka Clan.
***

And finally we reached the hill that overlooks the Nebulaka village. The child said goodbye to me with a happy face, and ran to the village.

I, Cadius, have fulfilled every wish that Travis VI, the Savior of the Kingdom, has ordered me to do as the Chief Wizard of Solisium.

Some call me cruel, but all these criticism mean nothing to me. I was loyal to my king, and my actions prove it.

Barbaric Trutizan shan't plague Solisium any longer, and their relics have been moved to a safer place. The Shrine of Devotion and Seal Sanctuary now have perfect security system, and everyone who participated to the process has been silenced - now no one know where the relic is except for me.

Turning the Royal Guards into Guardians was the best monumental achievement I have ever accomplished in my life. I thank them for their boundless devotion, and feel honored to help them so.

My last spell will cover the forest with everlasting fog, hiding all paths to the shrine. Then, I shall release every mana I have and slowly fade away amidst the fog.

My death will complete the mission. This island will be the proof of my absolute loyalty.

Cadius, Travis VI's Chief Wizard.

I was appointed as the best soldier in a mop-up campaign against Trutizan. That was why they sent me to the relic transportation squad.

We were supposed to move the royal relic to a shrine in a remote island, and I was very proud to be the part of this operation.

But right after we finished storing the last package, the Chief Wizard started to attack us. I thought something was off, and I ran away from the shrine with others. But the wizard came after us, and took us off one by one. He injured me as well, but I was not about to give up yet.

The wizard lashed another attack, and the ground I was standing collapsed.

The shock almost shattered me, but not bad enough to kill me. The wizard must have thought I was dead. He didn't come after me any further.

Then, fog crept in. I patched myself up sitting in the fog. My body ached all over, but what hurt me the most was the sense of betrayal. What the wizard did... was that an arbitrary action of his own? Or a planned attack?

I shook my head. The most important thing now was to leave this island alive. There must be someone at the dock. I stood up and looked around, but the fog was too thick. I could almost hear someone dragging something heavy in the fog. Maybe another survivor. I started to walk. The fog was getting thicker and thicker.

It was not a coincident that the Black Snake and Red Wings guilds came to Nebula Island at the same time. The dispute between the two guilds started when the Black Snake Guild leader Addler bore grudge against the Red Wings Guild leader Vernon, but no one knew the exact reasoning behind this. Vernon simply ignored Addler's provocation as the Black Snake was far smaller than the Red Wings, but such attitude worsened the animosity between the two guilds.

Addler used the Red Wings to explore Nebula Island. The Black Snake members silently stalked the Red Wings in the forest, while Red Wings did all the fighting with Orcs and treasure hunters, wasting their stamina and resources. In other words, the Red Wings were opening the road for the Black Snake for free.

The Red Wings' exploration went well. When Red Wings finally found the relic chest at the Shrine of Devotion, a huge group of bandits raided them. They were small fries compared to the Red Wings, and the guild won the battle at the end, but it left the most of guild members injured, including Vernon.

That's when Addler came in. That was the moment for Addler to get rid of the Red Wings once and for all, and take hold of the relic.

The first arrow hit one of the Red Wings. Then a hail of arrows stormed the rest of guild members and bandits. Some Red Wings members escaped the shrine, but remaining bandits were all killed. The Black Snake Guild took the relic with ease - it was a perfect hunt.

The Red Wings lost many members to the Black Snake, and was burning for revenge. Vernon was willing to do anything to annihilate the Black Snake Guild. The guild wizard Boldwin pointed at the Fog Forest on the map. Addler was an obsessive man, and it was certain that he would come after the remaining Red Wings if he knew where they were.

Boldwin suggested to set a trap in the Fog Forest, and spread the rumor that Vernon was critically injured and hiding in the said forest. When this rumor reached Addler's ear, he took off to the Fog Forest right away.

The forest was filled with thick fog. The vision was very bad, but all Addler could think of was killing Vernon, and he didn't mean to go back now.

Vernon and the Red Wings members hiding behind a gigantic tree was looking at the Black Snakes approach. Vernon thought they really looked like snakes. One of the Red Wings on the other tree sent a signal. Do we move in now? Everyone looked at Boldwin. At the same time, a Black Snake wizard stopped as if he felt something. Now!

Boldwin's blue lightnings hit the Black Snake guild. Vernon and his men jumped out of the blue sparkling fog, and started swinging swords. Vernon's red sword created a red haze. This time, it was a complete victory for the Red Wings.

It seems like bad luck follows me around.

I lost my way before, and now I'm lost again in the Fog Forest. I threw my grappling hook to find a way out, but it caught a Mitran.

Sigh... I don't know if I'll survive this time.

A tree appeared from the fog. The ugly crow scribbled on the tree was definitely mine. Oh no! I was so sure that I was heading forward, but I was keep walking in circles! I felt like I tried every direction. Poor me! I would have painted the town if I knew I was going to die like this.

Then I saw something sparkling ahead. When I got close, it was some sort of thread. Well, now that I think about it, it was stupid of me to touch it. But at that time, the thread seemed like the only way out of the forest.

I held the thread and carefully followed it. The thread became thicker and thicker as I moved forward. Then, I noticed a strange construction at the end of the rope. What was it called? The answer suddenly popped up in my head. A spider nest! And a huge one at that!

I screamed and ran to the opposite side. But it was another stupid mistake. It was as if I was loudly advertising fresh food to all monsters in the forest. I sensed more and more monsters coming after me. I kept running, but monsters never gave up neither.

I quickly searched my bag, and found the grappling hook. It took me some time, but I finally could throw the hook towards a large tree in front of me. Please, just catch anything, so that I could get out of here!

And the hook did grab a branch! But for some reason... it didn't feel right. Why is the tree moving? And why does this tree have a face? And it's glaring at me!
Oh I know now, I caught a Fog Mitran!

The Mitran seemed offended by my unexpected hair designing attempt. Maybe it would have forgiven me if I let go of the hook right away. Only... that I didn't. I held to the hook and ran.

My sudden move shocked Mitran, and made it go wild. So wild, that even monsters that have been chasing me had to leave. Some of them might have stayed, but I couldn't tell for sure. I was busy evading Mitran's attack.

Every time the Mitran smash the ground with its branch, I could feel my backpack shredding away. When the backpack completely gives up, it would be my back hitting the ground. I should have brought a stronger bag!

I threw myself to other trees to protect my back, but to no avail. The force was too great, and a single blow destroyed poor little trees.

I don't know how long it went on. After some time, I was pulled really hard by the rope in my hand and fell to the ground. I stood up and looked around, and you wouldn't believe what I saw. The Mitran, completely tied up with my rope, struggling to get up. I understood what happened. Every time Mitran whirled and turned, the rope on its head tangled up with its body.

I could see feathers, pieces of clothing, leaves, roots, bird nests, and every other forestry junk you could think of tangled up in the rope as well. What a hilarious sight! I should tell others about this! My guild friends won't believe me, but I have the proof right here! Now no one will call me a fool anymore.

Then I heard my Guild leader calling my name, and Guild members complaining. I began to run with a big smile on my face.

There used to be a rumor among adventurers that Solisium royalty hid something precious in the Nebula Island. And I didn't overlook them as a mere gossip, because of the story of Balogan, an old man I happened to meet on the street.

Balogan used to be a famous builder, and always talked about horrors he witnessed when he was working at Nebula Island. At first I thought it was a senile old man's blabber, but his story was oddly specific and coherent.

So I, Cohen, decided to follow his story to Nebula Island, which was a natural thing to do for a renowned travel writer. I even found the worker's lodging Balogan told me, and its front yard was filled with old neglected tombstones.

When I was sketching the yard and tombstones, a woman approached me and begged me to help her finding her child. I felt it was strange, but the woman seemed desperate and I couldn't refuse her.

She sad the child must have fallen asleep among tombstones, so I went out to search. But what I found was a small pile of bones. When I talked to the woman again, she sobbed and began to tell me a story:

Her husband used to be a famous builder. One day, he was summoned by the king to Nebula Island for some project, and she never heard from him again. So the woman went to the island with her child to find her husband. But all she did find was an abandoned lodging and weird tombstones around the house. She got scared and try to leave, but lost her way in the fog and perished with her child at the end.

Then the woman disappeared. I made a sketch of her face in my journal, and went back to Balogan. I explained Balogan what happened on the island, and when I showed him the drawing, he cried. He said it was her wife.

I wrote a book about Balogan family, as a way of showing my condolences to them. But for some unknown reason, my publication was banned.

I smelled something fish about it, so I changed my name and left home. Years passed, and when I was staring to think about going back home, I heard the news that Balogan has passed away.

When I went to his funeral, people who recognized my face told me about Balogan. One of these stories was that Balogan was very thorough in hiding his past. I realized that he would have never told me about Nebula Island if he didn't go senile.

In the end, I completely gave up on going back to my home. And what happened to me at the Nebula Island, I would never forget.

I have been leading the guild all my life, and there were bright and dark moments. I had friends and foes, but what waited for me at the end of the road was betrayal and despair. I hope my experience helps you to avert the tragedy that I am experiencing now.

1. Do not shun those who give you candid advice
My first mistake was to ignore the advice from my old friend Rotreck. I willingly blinded myself by ignoring his words.

2. Know what is loyalty and what is deception
What the betrayer Jerome has shown me was false loyalty. Know that true loyalty comes from actions, not sweet words.

3. Do not trust people you don't know well
I trusted Jerome and his men too easily, and it led me to destruction. Remember that trust is something that builds over time.

4. Kind actions can be deceptive
Jerome guarded me, brought me food and treasure only because it served his purpose. Know that kind actions from others could blind you.

5. Don't be afraid to doubt
I didn't doubt Jerome, because I chose to believe what I wanted to believe. Remember, some healthy amount of suspicion could help you to go a long way.

6. Don't let your emotion sway your decisions
Jerome's sweet words made me happy, and it affected my decisions. Decisions should be made based on logic, not emotions.

7. Do not mistake your friend's advice as mischief-making
When Rotreck told me of Jerome's conspiracy, I called Rotreck a mischief-maker. I was warned, yet I chose to ignore it and it destroyed me.

8. Do not neglect your old friends over new faces
When I took in Jerome and his men, I neglected Rotreck and my old friends in the guild. Know that trust only comes from those who stayed with you in trying times.

9. Power reveals a man's character
What Jerome did for me during the difficult times was not about helping me, but using me. And when he got the power, he chose to stab me in the back. Know that power reveals a man's character.

10. Honorable man keeps his words
Rotreck fought for me with his life until the end. An honorable man will keep his words, no matter what hardships he may face.
