In my quest to uncover the hidden history of Nebula Island, I met an old man in a tavern through a tip. He gave me a surprising testimony.
Mr. Marcellos, can you tell me about when you went to Nebula Island and what you did there?

(Coughing) Th-that was the day that everything went wrong for me. A group of stonemasons were summoned. I was one of them. (Clears throat) We... Erm... We had a special assignment from the court wizard. It was a royal order. Who could disobey King Travis? Besides, the wizard said there would be a great reward. We took him at his word and boarded the ship.
When we arrived at the fog-shrouded island, the whole place was filled with something eerie and strange. We went underground, and there... There stood these terrifying stone soldiers. They had no souls, but I could sense some sort of murderous energy from them. My task was to repair them, and I, well, I did my best. (Coughing) Little did I know... it was a trap.

Did something bad happen? Can you tell me about what happened?

(Clears throat) The day all the work was done, the court wizard threw a celebration for us. The air in the banquet hall was strangely heavy.
I couldn't shake a feeling of unease, so I went to do a final inspection of the stone soldiers I had repaired, and... (Coughing) The great hall where the soldiers were gathered was empty. Suddenly I heard screams coming from the banquet hall. I-I ran toward it. As I was running, screams filled my ears, and I saw...
My colleagues were lying there, covered in blood. The stone soldiers were searching for survivors like demonic machines, and behind them was the court wizard. With an expressionless look on his face, he was barking orders to the soldiers and counting the bodies. In that moment, everything became clear. He planned to kill us all when we were finished. I frantically fled, even risking a leap off a cliff into the sea. The waves threatened to swallow me up, but I felt I'd be better off drowning. I was tossed around by the waves and luckily rescued by a merchant ship passing nearby, but I've never been the same since... It's a nightmare I can't escape.

I can't imagine how traumatizing that event must have been. It's unbelievable. But why do you think the wizard did what he did at the time?

I... (Coughing) I still don't know the exact reason, but I do know that those stone soldiers weren't just defending our kingdom. They were trying to hide or protect something on the island. Everything we saw on the island was a reason for us to die.
I was just a stonemason. Polishing stones was all I did. But it led me and my colleagues into tragedy, and now I'm... I'm a drunken beggar with nothing.
I want to know the truth, but I'm afraid it will threaten me again. I shudder at the memory of it... Maybe it would have been better if I had ended up in that sea. (Coughing)
Now that I've told you everything I can remember, can you buy me another drink?
Before I could stop him, he gave me a brief smile and unleashed a powerful spell.

A Fateful Event

When I first entered Venelux School of Magic, Elior was a world away from the other students. His calm, cool demeanor, keen insight, and genius magical skills made him the pride of the professors, always at the top of his class, while I was the one on the other side of the room, always in the spotlight for my bumbling mistakes. I was always failing Transformation, and I was always getting into trouble.
Then, one day, something catastrophic happened. During my Transformation test, I accidentally turned my proctor into a gargoyle. As the proctor turned to stone and became a flying, ceiling-hovering horror, the testing room erupted into chaos, and the gargoyle locked eyes with me and charged at me with deadly intent. Just as I thought I was dead, someone stepped in front of the gargoyle and calmly chanted. "Arcanis Umbriel Dispello!" It was Elior, his courageous voice and decisive gesture still clear in my mind. While everyone else was in a state of confusion, Elior turned the giant stone monster back into a human being with his magic, and the incident ended with Elior's wisdom and courage. After that day, Elior and I became close friends. But I didn't realize then how important this event was to me.

To Nebula Island

As the years passed, we went our separate ways. Elior graduated from the magic school and went on to higher studies as a wizard, while I utilized my aptitude for swordsmanship to become a magical swordsman. Years later, I sought to join a guild adventuring on Nebula Island, where I was reunited with Elior, who was the guild leader. A man of both magic and wisdom, Elior had grown into a man entirely worthy of leading a guild. My joy at seeing him again was indescribable, and we greeted each other as if we had returned to our childhood. With our morale boosted by the presence of so many talented guild members, we finally set out for Nebula Island.
Our journey to Nebula Island, however, was difficult from day one. Filled with traps and monsters, the island was a living hell, and our guild members fell one by one. By the time we reached the Seal Sanctuary, most of the guild had already been sacrificed. When the remaining guild members were exhausted from fatigue and fear, the worst crisis came when the giant stone soldiers appeared. The overwhelming power of the stone soldiers crushed us, until only I and Elior were left standing.

A Struggle in Despair

In the tense moment, Elior seemed to make a final decision. Before I could stop him, he gave me a brief smile and unleashed a powerful spell. It was a deadly spell that froze everything around him. As a bright light emanated from his hand, his body began to stiffen. I can still see Elior turning to stone. I can still see the look of determination and courage on his face as he gave everything to save his friend. I couldn't let it end there. I opened the magic tome he left behind and studied it, desperate to bring him back to life. It was full of incomprehensible words, but his last smile kept me going.
I figured out almost everything, but I couldn't find the final execution spell anywhere. In despair, I stared at his stone mouth and suddenly remembered the spell that Elior had chanted as a boy to turn back the gargoyle. "Arcanis Umbriel Dispello!"
I repeated the spell at Elior, and a miracle happened. The light of life slowly began to return to Elior's petrified body. His hands began to move, and finally he was whole again. We hugged each other and shed tears; he had restored most of the guild, and we had found the artifact, bringing our adventure to a perfect conclusion. Looking back, I realize that the miracle that saved us from despair was not a coincidence, but a product of friendship.

The king rubbed his forehead and sighed deeply. For if the relic of the Sanctuary were ever to be stolen, his immortal soldiers alone would not be able to retrieve it. At that moment, the chief wizard took a step closer to the king and spoke a meaningful word.
"Your Majesty, I know of one way to remove your anxiety. To have the most capable soldiers in the kingdom guard the relic forever." The king's eyes shone with determination to protect the relic. "If you mean by the most capable soldiers...?" The chief wizard replied without pause. "Yes, that's right. The Royal Guard."
Hearing those words sent a chill down my spine. What he was proposing was black magic that would trap people's souls in armor, forcing them to perform blind acts. Worst of all, in the Royal Guard was my son, Elio. I desperately objected, but I could not sway the king's determination to protect the relic.

That night, I went to the chief wizard and pleaded with him. "Please, let me take my son's place. Please, you can't kill my son. He's just come of age and has been made a Guard." But the chief wizard shook his head. "Everyone else is in the same situation, Deputy Wizard. No one is exempt." At that moment, a mixture of anger and despair welled up inside me. Nonetheless, I could not give up on my son.
I went straight to Elio, and engraved the highest level of dispel magic schema into his armor. That way, even if Elio became a ghost in his armor, the spell would activate immediately and he would return to his original self after three days. In the meantime, I would have to steal away my ghostly son and wait for him to return. To my son, trembling with the knowledge of his fate, I promised hope and left.

The hope was short-lived, however. The next day, the chief wizard began removing all the enchantment schemas from the Guards' armor, claiming that they needed to perform the ritual in their purest state. When it was Elio's turn, the chief wizard glanced at me and erased all of the schematics from his armor, and just like that, my last hope for dispel magic was gone.
Then, the chief wizard's ritual began in earnest. "Now, you will become the eternal guardians of the relic." I attempted to break into the ritual, but was quickly stopped. One by one, the soldiers of the Guard, writhing in agony under the power of black magic, fell to the ground, and then, their empty armor slowly rose to their feet.
I called out my son's name desperately to the empty armor, but all that came back was the cold clink of metal against metal. He was no longer responding to my voice.

I was brought before the king for disrupting the ritual. The king did not forgive me. I was stripped of all my powers as Deputy Wizard, and I was thrown into prison. I was scheduled to be executed with the other prisoners at daybreak. But I had to survive somehow to get my son back.
While bound hand and foot, I deliberately drew a magic schema with my blood to escape the prison and left the island in a small sailboat. As I drifted out to sea, I looked back at the island, where my son remained, a cursed armor to protect the artifact. "Elio, I swear to you. I will return to rescue you..." As I drifted through the cold waters, I came close to death several times, but my resolve to bring my son back only grew stronger. Until I reached shore, that promise was the only thing holding me alive.
There was a foul-smelling, sticky green slime on the floor. Just when I thought something must have spilled over, a sudden chill ran down my spine.

Since I began my adventuring career, I had never ventured out with so many others before. Ever since my brief encounter with the goblin merchant a few days ago, my mind had been filled with thoughts of Nebula Island. Nebula Island, he said, was where the treasures of a lost age were hidden. Clearly, something hidden on Nebula Island was calling to me. My companions expressed apprehension, but I stood firm in their midst. As adventurers, we must test our insatiable curiosity and courage, right?
We finally arrived at Nebula Island, where our first encounter was with a group of possessed armor soldiers called the Ancient Guardians. Chills ran down my spine as I fended off their razor-sharp blades, and during our battle with them, we nearly fell again and again. This island was certainly a fearsome place, worthy of legend. After defeating all of the Guardians, we found a mysterious portal and entered without hesitation to claim the treasure.

The place we entered through the portal was a dark altar with an ominous aura. We slowly walked around the altar and noticed a strange substance on the floor. It was a sticky, light-greenish liquid. Something about it made my stomach turn, but I didn't have time to realize it was an ominous sign.
Suddenly, out of the darkness, a giant eyeball stared down at us. The eye with tentacles reminded me of the name Exodus I had heard from the goblin. Light began to pour out of the center of that demonic eye, and in an instant, my guild members fell to the ground. All around me, screams and shock erupted into chaos, and the horrific eyeball now pounded the ground, sending powerful waves. Cries of pain broke out here and there, and more than half of my companions died on the spot.

The gaze of Exodus drove us into a hell of despair. Everything seemed to end in an instant. I was on my knees on the ground, clutching my sword. No anger or vengeance filled me, only a fear that seemed to freeze me in place.
The survivors gathered together and attempted to escape, but I was unable to do anything as fear overcame all judgment. I barely made it out alive with the help of my companions. Even now, days later, as I write this journal, I feel fear occupying my mind rather than vengeance, and every night I have nightmares of my companions dying over and over again.
What is it that I need now: a fight, revenge, or simply to forget the memories of the cursed island that I never want to be reminded of again?

"Well, this is easy!" Ricky said confidently, reaching for the sanctuary's relic. Beside him, Nina looked around nervously and whispered. "Ricky, something always goes wrong when you say that..."
Ricky shrugged off Nina's warning and held up the relic. "If we sell this, we'll be rich! Hahaha!" But before Ricky could stop laughing, the relic radiated light and the sound of metal clashing could be heard.
Nina's eyes widened. She shook Ricky's arm. "Wh-what was that? Put that thing down!" I turned my head to see the Ancient Guardians coming toward us. White-faced, I shouted. "What are you doing? RUN!"
We ran, the Ancient Guardians closing in behind us. Ricky was gasping for breath but talking nonstop. "Aren't Ancient Guardians supposed to be slow?" Nina shouted, sweating profusely. "Oh, shut up and run!"
Ah, why did I ever trust these idiots and get involved in this? Regret washed over me.

Am I going to die like this? I came here with my friends to try to steal something for the first time, and this is how I end up? I yelled at Ricky. "Ricky, drop the relic! You're going to kill us all if you hold on to it!" But Ricky couldn't let go. "You want me to let go of it? It's worth a fortune!"
Just then, one of the Ancient Guardians slammed his heavy sword down on Ricky, who screamed and rolled sideways to avoid it. Nina shouted desperately. "Our lives are more important than money, you idiot!" As Ricky flinched, I added. "Ricky, throw that relic, or we're all dead!"
Ricky finally made up his mind and threw the relic at an Ancient Guardian, which landed squarely on its head with a clang, and the Ancient Guardians instantly froze in place.
And just like that, we had escaped. Catching her breath, Nina said with a serious look on her face. "Ricky, we have to stop. We're not going to live long if we keep doing this." Ricky smiled sheepishly, scratching his head. "Okay, okay, I'll be more careful next time." Nina glared. Only then, he swore there would be no next time.
The three of us stared at each other in silence for a moment, and then burst out laughing at the joy of being alive. It was time to get back to our lives. Ricky and Nina would never dream of stealing again... Maybe.

The last sentence of the King's letter echoed in my head.

"As your king, I command you: if you are truly loyal, carry out my orders even in death."

Tonight, I received a letter from the King. Until I broke the seal, I expected it to be just another mission. But when I opened it, it took my breath away.

"Tomorrow, at dusk, you and your men will be reborn as guardians of the Royal Relic. This will be the most honorable duty given to the Guard, for true loyalty does not end with death."

The King's handwriting on the parchment weighed heavily on me. His message was clear: my men and I were to become ghosts and guard the royal relic forever. My heart raced, and I found it difficult to breathe.

I had lived as his loyal sword, giving everything for him and his orders. I was ready to die for him at any moment.

But to be stripped of all sense of life and freedom, to be left only as a soul, to guard a relic for all eternity? I would have preferred to die, but that was a fate I could not choose.

What weighed me down further was that I had to tell this to my men. My hands trembled as I stared at the letter. If I tore it up, if I sent my men fleeing... No, I can't. I would be a criminal, hunted by the Royal Army for the rest of my life.

One by one, the faces of my men came to mind, and my heart sank. They had traveled the battlefields with the King, deprived of seeing their families, but filled with pride as members of the Royal Guard.

For a long time, I froze in place, my head hung low. It was time to make a decision: as Captain of the Guard, I must tell my men of the cruel fate that awaits us. If I must bear the inevitable fate, at least I must do so without shame. With a final resolve, I slowly raised my head.

The old man staggered toward the Guardians. With the eerie sound of clanging metal, the Guardians approached the old man, who was looking for his son among them.
Looking at the old man's back, I remembered the days I had spent with him. He was my mentor. He was deep in the mountains, alone and absorbed in his studies, when he found and healed me after I was severely injured while practicing magic. I recognized his magical prowess and, after much begging, became his apprentice.
For thirty years, Master devoted himself to a single study. He never spoke of his past or personal history, and he never told me the purpose of his research. But on the day the experiment he was certain would succeed failed, he revealed for the first time that his work was to bring back his son, who had become a cursed wraith.
And not long ago, Master's last experiment also ended in failure. The magic schema always failed when it was on the verge of completion. The aging Master realized that he didn't have much time left, so he abandoned his research. He instead climbed aboard a ship to see his son one last time before he died.

Even though he insisted on going alone, I followed him and we arrived at a remote, unnamed island. When I realized that he intended to make it his last place, and tried to dissuade him, he shook his head with determination.
He pushed me away from him, and walked alone toward the Guardians. He barely fended off their attacks while trying to locate his son. I wanted to help him, but I could not sway his resolve.
Suddenly a smile spread across his wrinkled face. Though he was nothing but armor, without a face or body, Master seemed to recognize his son. In the brief silence that followed, Master breathed his last and died. And the Guardian, presumably his son, stood frozen in place, as if mourning the death of the old man.
I realized that the story of Master and Guardian, their story was not yet finished. It was clear that his death had touched something beyond the Guardian's cold armor. I vowed to continue my master's research, believing that this would be the clue to a new beginning.

I was trapped in a collapsing labyrinth as I pored over the schema extracted from the book containing demonic knowledge.
Lady Calanthia was observing me for a while, and after taking but a single glance at the schema, she was able to see right through their logic.
As she waved her hand in the air, the three schema from the demonic tomes came together in the air.
As I stood witness to her miracle, I could not hold back my tears.

17th Copy: Record of Lady Calanthia's Youth

An ominous star shone that night.
Roen, the daughter of Mark Aron, the Lord of Belphoret, was born. On the back of her hands, the black wings of Sylaveth appeared, an omen of the disaster to come. Shocked by what he saw, Lord Aron called Greedal, the royal guardian wizard.
He advised, "To banish this curse, it must be transferred to a child who was born simultaneously with Roen."
The lord's soldiers discovered a baby in a small village who matched the date and time description. After murdering her resistant parents, they kidnapped the baby.

The child who bore the curse would later be named 'Calanthia.'

31st Copy: Record of Audience with His Majesty Reville Lupius

When Greedal, enfeebled from failing to absorb Sylaveth's mana, visited the girl, she was curled up in a dark corner of the room, dressed in rags.
She had absorbed all the mana from a necklace that Greedal had given her, and her eyes now bore a certain purple dark glow. She clenched her fist tightly and her abusive adoptive parents instantly burnt to crisp.

Overjoyed after witnessing this power, Greedal brought her to His Majesty right away grinning from ear to ear.

His Majesty bestowed upon her the name 'Calanthia' after the way her eyes shined in the darkness. The girl, having felt warmth and recognition for her existence for the first time, swore loyalty to him then and there.

48th Copy: Record of the Execution of the Lord of Belphoret

After conquering Belphoret, Lady Calanthia lifted each member of the lord's family in the air and incinerated them.
Lord Mark Aron's dying screams filled the square. He was executed last after being forced to watch his family burn alive.
After his screaming stopped, Lady Calanthia held an empty stare. His Majesty Reville Lupius, after a momentary consideration, ordered her to make the witnessing crowd laugh and dance by force.
As Lady Calanthia's magic spread throughout the crowd, they began to dance and sing like mindless puppets, and the bloody square soon turned into a grotesque festival.
His Majesty spotted Roen, the daughter of the lord, who managed to be the only one unaffected by the enchantment. The soldiers gave chase immediately, but were unable to capture her.

Resurrected Fossil

When Lady Calanthia stopped in front of the ruined palace,
a fossil of an ancient dragon, posed as if it were roaring at the sky, suddenly came to life with her touch.

A purple bolt of lightning struck its ashen scales as she uttered "It will make for a nice guard dog...". The ruins shook as the once dead dragon took a deep breath.

Dragaryle is its name, the first of her Constructs, resurrected through her will.

Incarnate of Rage and Ruthlessness

Lady Calanthia gathered the Star Fragment's magic in her fingertips and drew a line in the air, and the ruined palace's floor was covered in fire and ice, and two shapes were formed.

The one whose rage burns fiercely was given the name 'Vulkan', as it was the incarnation of Lady Calanthia's fury.

The other could extinguish light with icy silence and was called 'Zairos', as Calanthia's chilling calmness shaped its power.

They were both a single anathema formed out of her abyssal power, a singular force yet opposite to each other.

Even as I was being chased by monsters, I managed to narrow down where the suspicious sound was coming from. I really hope it's one of these three spots... At this rate, I'll end up getting torn apart by those hideous imps. Ugh, maybe I should just ditch this whole thing and say I'm out...

It's me, Antonio, the pathetic debtor.
Remember what you said to me the other day? You said that I would never live to grow old if I kept chasing after money. I scoffed and called you melodramatic. Now, if I could go back to that day, I'd double, no, increase my debts a thousandfold.
To be honest, I didn't want to take this job in the first place. I mean, who would enter Lequirus's Den to search for a nobleman's lost belongings? I'd been wandering around for a while when I heard the terrible scream of a beast. I quickly ducked behind a rock, only to come face to face with a creature that I shouldn't even call Lequirus anymore. That monstrous behemoth, towering over a mountain of ants, of blood and venom... Fortunately, I don't remember much after the first attack, except that it hurt like hell.
You know, I've always wanted to ask you to watch the sun set over Vienta Vineyard with me someday. Is that too cheesy? Cut me some slack. It's my last wish. I'm slowly dissolving into a pool of venom from my legs up.
Purplo, to tell you the truth... I'm in so much pain... I know I'll die if I fall asleep now, but... I can't keep my eyes open...

Chapter 1: The Tragedy of the Casill Family

In order to prevent the overflow of Mauvessence in my body, I arrived at Kastleton in search of Martinay Casill. It is said that this village, which appears peaceful on the surface, once suffered a terrible incident in the past. Will I be able to meet Martinay here and deal with the mana frenzy?

The cursed rain fell because Martinay's sister, Adriana, was unable to overcome the threat of Arkeum in the past. Since that day, she suffered the pains of Mana Frenzy, and her sister's medicine provided no relief. In the end, she decided to leave hoping to escape the clutches of Arkeum, who sought her Star Fragment. The note she left behind said that controlling her strength was the only way to relieve the torment from the Mana Frenzy.
Chapter 2: The Demise of the Gray-Fanged

Ten years ago, a pack of Wolves led by Iskale the Gray-Fanged took over the Blackhowl Plains and drove the town into a state of constant terror. What actually happened the night that the wicked wolf perished? Many people in Kastleton still remember the events of that day.

It was the courage of a young man that led to the defeat of Iskale the Gray-Fanged, who threatened Kastleton. Henry, the lord's son, fought Iskale alone and sacrificed his life to protect the town he loved. The Wolf Hunting Contest is still held in the Blackhowl Plains to honor Henry, the hero, to this day.

I helped the Contract Manager and began carrying out Resistance Contracts. While carrying out various contracts in many lands from Kastleton to the Starlight Observatory Ruins, I learned that the goblins in Urstella Fields were acting suspiciously. Just what are those Goblins up to?

Ten years ago, Henson, the former Watch Captain, defended the Starlight Observatory Ruins in the battle against Arkeum. The fight cost him his eye and many comrades. Henson blamed himself and resigned from his position as captain. With the Starlight Observatory facing another crisis, Henson, a veteran of countless battles, charged right into the conflict.
Chapter 4: The Terrific Trio of Carmine Forest

In a corner of the Starlight Observatory square, a Diston similar to Lunar-0 was asking for help. This Diston was left behind by the young wizard Rutaine, who urgently requested I come to Carmine Forest. What could be behind this urgent message?

The Arkeum Legion kidnapped children from all over the country to gain the power of the Star Fragments. You helped the Terrific Trio raid the Arkeum's hideout after a pursuit, joining forces there with the heroic Captain DaVinci. In the end, the children were safely rescued, and Arkeum's plot was once again crushed by the Resistance.
Chapter 5: A Sacred Pledge of Blood

The unnamed epidemic beginning to spread through Vienta Village plunged this peaceful town into chaos. Residents were expelled to an isolation facility outside of town, and with contact with epidemic patients cut off, their relatives anxiously waited for news. Where did this mysterious plague begin?

A dark truth lurked behind the Vienta Village epidemic. The Vampire Leonardas, disguised as a kind healer, spread the false epidemic to sneak away patients for a terrible Blood Ritual. Sophia was also in danger of becoming a Ghoul, but the power of the Vampire Slayer Ezekiel imbued in a Guardian's Pledge was able to save her. Guardian Ezekiel was Leonardas's old foe and was finally able to get the revenge he hadn't achieved in life through the magic of the Guardian's Pledge.
Chapter 6: The Song of the Vienta Dwarves

A long time ago, the Resistance members who joined forces with the residents of Stonegard drove out the tyrant Fernan and the Arkeum factions who were exploiting the residents. Although there is peace now, Resistance forces are still secretly working in Vienta Village to prevent the frequent incursions of Arkeum factions.

In the past, Sienna Parsons and her companions brought a giant Golem to drive a tyrant out of Stonegard Castle. The Golem's Heart, which the Arkeum Wizards sought, was the power source that moved that giant Golem long ago⁠—it was a Manastone that bore the power of a Star Fragment.
The Song of the Vienta Dwarves

He was once a warrior who fought bravely to protect his home from Queen Bellandir, the Sandstorm Overlord. However, his sole aim now is to prevent his daughter from taking up his mantle in the battle versus Queen Bellandir. Just how terrible a monster is Queen Bellandir that a dead father's soul feels the need to remain here?

Up to that point, Roen Aron was the only human to ever defeat Queen Bellandir. But now a new name would have to be added to the record. Marcia Richill, Sandworm Raid Group Captain, successfully lured in Queen Bellandir and dealt her a deadly blow. Behind her success was a man who worried about his daughter, even after death, and the member of the Resistance who aided his cause.

In the Manawastes, the main site of the anomalies, the forbidden conjuring techniques of Shadowmancers have been found. Her goal was to defeat Havres, the Demon of Knowledge, and take the fragment of the Star of Sylaveth for herself. Thanks to her deception, I was taken advantage of and almost lost my life. In the end, however, I managed to defeat Demon Risieth.
Chapter 9: A Pact of Fire and Darkness

A Pact of Fire and Darkness

The Arkeum Legion took people with Star Fragments through nightmares to create a Giant Star Fragment. Kazar hindered the Resistance's escape, but they managed to escape thanks to Clay's sacrifice. We still need greater strength to fight against Kazar.

The Resistance has been searching for Clay since he went missing, but has found no leads so far. Meanwhile, Rutaine at the Purelight Tower asks for your help to repair Clay's Diston Lunar-0. The repaired Lunar-0 said that Janice Cartair is capable enough to chase down Clay. Lunar-0 asked me to find her as she is in Talandre.

Have you heard of the Startree Solstice, Solisium's yearly winter tradition? Once upon a time, Solisium and Trutizan were at war. The war continued through the frigid winter months. The tired soldiers were cold and hungry.
One day, an old woman in a red robe appeared and handed out freshly baked cookies to all the soldiers of Solisium and Trutizan. The hitherto expressionless soldiers smiled as they received the warm cookies. They called the cookie-giving grandmother the "Gift Grandmother," and the story spread far and wide. <np>
Inspired by her story, people hung food, clothes, and other items from a large tree to comfort those who were worse off because of the war. When a wizard saw their noble act, he enchanted the top of the tree to glow so that the gifts could be seen from far away. The people called this glowing, decorated tree the Startree because it shone like a star.
This sparked a moment of peace among the people, and soon after, the war ended. Since then, Solisium has celebrated the Startree Solstice every winter.

Long ago, people believed that specters who died of hunger envied the living and ruined the harvest.
 On the year when the harvest was ruined, they put a scary-looking specter mask on a scarecrow and performed a ritual of beating it and setting it on fire to scare the specters away.
However, after a couple of years, crops would always wilt despite performing the ritual. The villagers blamed the Chief Priest and tried to kill him. Then he proposed to comfort the specters instead of scaring them.<np>
The people wore smiling pumpkin masks, pretending to be specters, and visited all the houses in the village. The villagers welcomed them into their homes. The specters, mixed among the people, were comforted thanks to the warm welcome.
The year after, the harvest was plentiful. Since then, people have worn costumes to visit all the houses in the village for snacks and dispel any bad energy in their homes. That was the beginning of the famous autumn event of Solisium, the Haunted Harvest.

The Startree Solstice stems from a beautiful tradition that blossomed during a harsh war.
During the war between Solisium and Trutizan, soldiers on both sides were cold and hungry.
One day, an old woman in red robes appeared. Confused, the soldiers quickly raised their weapons, but the old woman was unperturbed. She began handing out cookies to soldiers on both sides.
Her kindness soon warmed the hearts of the soldiers, and the story touched the hearts of many.<np>From then on, people called her "Gift Grandma" and followed her lead, preparing gifts for those suffering from war. They hung the gifts on a large tree for anyone to take home.
No one took up arms around the tree. After a wizard shone a light at the top to lead others to the tree, it became known as the Startree.
The war ended soon after, and people continue to remember the past and share their warmth every winter with the Startree Solstice.

The origin of the Haunted Harvest began with a wish for a plentiful harvest by consoling the dead who died from hunger, preventing them from becoming dangerous specters.
Long ago, people couldn't predict the weather or the seasons, and a bad harvest could mean life or death for an entire village. In years of plentiful harvest, they held a thanksgiving ceremony, while in years of famine, they blamed the specters and scared them off by destroying and burning scarecrows.
<np>The Chief Priest pleaded with the villagers to console the specters instead of intimidating them. Though many were skeptical, desperate farmers finally tried dressing up like specters and wandered the town. The villagers welcomed all guests, living and dead, with warm hearts. The visiting spirits were consoled by their heartfelt prayers, and were able to move on. Ever since then, farmers associate this festival with a good harvest.
Holding a festival and ritual for the dead and the harvest became a tradition, which evolved into what is currently known as the Haunted Harvest.

Known as a symbol of peace, the Startree Solstice stems from a beautiful tradition of hanging gifts on trees during wartime for people to take with them, regardless of faction.
Long ago, Solisium and Trutizan were at war. The fighting continued into the winter, and soldiers on both sides grew cold and hungry.
An old woman in red robes, later dubbed "Gift Grandmother," baked cookies and distributed them to both camps. The soldiers, who had been pointing their weapons at her, suddenly felt warmed by the cookies.<np>
After the story of the gift-giving grandmother spread, some noble people hung food, clothes, and socks on a large tree for those who were suffering more than they were, regardless of faction.
A wizard saw this and shone a light at the top of the tree so that people could find it from a distance, and people began to call it the Startree.
No one drew their weapons around the Startree, and the war ended shortly thereafter. Since then, people have gathered every winter to remember the past and share their warmth at the Startree Solstice.

People once believed that the souls of those who had died of starvation despised the living. Jealous of their good harvests, these lonely ghosts sought to cause famine and flooding.
In years of bad harvests, the people made scarecrows with heads made of rotten crops and beat or burned them, trying to scare these specters away.
Soon, even this ritual didn't seem to work. After years of famine, the people turned on the Chief Priest. In desperation, the Chief Priest proposed a less violent, if unorthodox, ritual.<np>
For one night, the priest told the villagers to wear masks and visit the homes of their neighbors, and to give a warm welcome to all.
Observing this, the curious specters mingled among the living villagers, and were comforted by their generosity. After a night of celebration, the famine miraculously ended, and the villagers enjoyed plentiful food after years of hardship.
Since then, the people have held a similar ritual every year, as a warm welcome to the spirits and as thanks for an abundant harvest.

The Haunted Harvest is one of Solisium's most beloved celebrations. It's known as a night of costumes and sweet candy, where gleeful screams and laughter fill the autumn air. However, few know that the festival started thanks to one priest's unusual proposal.
In the past, farmers believed that malicious specters who envied the living were ruining their harvest year after year. Fearing for their crops, they held a ritual to ward off these nasty spirits. But, despite their fervent attempts to chase these specters away, the bad harvests continued. It was then that a clever High Priest had an idea: perform a ritual to calm the spirits instead.<np>
Willing to try anything, one local priest instructed the villagers to wear masks and act like specters. The masks were carved from pumpkins, a seasonal favorite to symbolize a bountiful harvest. These masked villagers would mingle with any spirits, and any nighttime visitors would be welcomed warmly and given gifts.
And just like that, unending bad harvest ended. This once humble ritual has since grown into a full-blown festival, a celebration of generosity, bountiful harvests, and good-hearted pranks.

Isn't it a little spooky when the sky turns red like this?
Some people have the power of rain at their disposal.
That's some tough-looking equipment. If only human bodies were that strong...
Don't get comfortable with the beasts. They'll eat you alive if you let your guard down!
The beasts have better night vision than us, so you should be careful if you're going hunting.
What's with the weather? I don't like it.
What is this rainstorm? Did someone cause it with magic?
Competition is strong in the Wolf Hunting Contest.
I've come a long way just to join the Wolf Hunting Contest!
You should go inside and rest at night. Don't underestimate the wild animals.
You see it too, right? The sky turned dark all of a sudden!
Everyone's here for the Hunting Contest.
Are you going to join the Hunting Contest, too?
Don't overdo it while you're hunting, and take it easy when you need to. That's the sort of hunter that lasts the longest.
Damn it, why is it raining? I hate rain.
You can see the beasts better in the snow. It's a great opportunity for hunters.
That's an awesome weapon! You won't need to worry.
Can you share any secrets for hunting wolves?
Are you going to join the Hunting Contest, too? That means I don't stand a chance...
If you hunt together with your guild members, you won't have to fear even the strongest beasts!
Watch out for the goblins. They're fast.
There are dangerous places all around here. Be careful when you're going out at night.
Darn. I should have brought a raincoat.
I knew this would happen. That's why I dressed warm today.
Look at how dark it got!
Can I take a look at your weapon? Where did you get it?
You're in a guild? I'm so jealous.
Can I help you? Just let me know.
Let me know if you need dinner or anything else.
What would you like to order? Something to warm you up from the snow?
It's raining again? I should clean the floor.
I can do business safely now that Laslan is free. I just hope this peace lasts.
Time flies. I should hurry up and prepare dinner.
When it's snowing, it's best to stay inside and warm up.
If your clothes are wet, you can dry them off in front of the fire. There's no charge for that!
Mana may be invisible, but it's always around us.
True magic is from Venelux. Civilian magic pales in comparison.
Humans have a short memory, but history is recorded in the flow of mana.
I've got a headache after focusing all day long.
This rain... What sort of magic is this?
This isn't typical magic. Could it be related to the elemental spirits?
When I was young, I used to think life would be amazing if I became a wizard.
Have you heard of Harvesters? They're fascinating dolls that help wizards with their research.
Night has fallen. I should light up some candles.
I came from Venelux to investigate the Wasteland and strengthen the barrier.
The monsters here are dangerous. Don't let your guard down.
The air feels fresh since it's raining.
There's magic inside that little doll accompanying you.
I'm not sure if this experiment is a success or failure...
You just watch. I'm going to research magic that will make history one day.
Huh? When did the sun set?
The sky is red? This magic must be...
It's raining again! My cloak's going to get all wet.
I hope the snow doesn't pile up...
Humans contaminated the earth with war, so it's our responsibility to purify it.
Did you see the dead land of the Ruins of Turayne? It's the sorrowful vestiges left behind by war.
It only takes an instant to destroy something, while it takes hundreds of years to rebuild.
I'm doing my best to teach the trainees, but they're falling way behind in comparison to Venelux.
I'm sorry, but I'm a bit busy with my research.
Why are the young wizard trainees so lazy these days?!
Do you have any questions about magic?
It's pretty late. Do you have business in the tower?
The trees of the forest become stronger when it's raining. Be careful.
Hello, ^<c=@MK_D_Dialogue>{gva_PcName}^</c>. What brings you to the Purelight Tower?
Why are you here? The Purelight Tower isn't for people like you.
After work, you have to wind down with a drink!
What? You got somethin' to say?
I'm all done with work, so I should head home.
Quit loitering and go your way.
I can protect you at night if you have the money, but there's no need for that...
It's not good to be nosy.
You should think before you strike up a conversation with just anyone. I hate getting interrupted.
You won't see prices like this anywhere else! Take a look at what we have!
You're not going to die, just to get your hands on some Sollant, right? Nothing is worth more than your life!
Oh, I should start heading home.
All my goods will be ruined because of the rain!
As if business wasn't already slow... Now it's snowing?
Check if you're missing anything before you take off. Laslan is bigger than you think.
The more consumables, the better. Don't you think so?
Goodness, would you look at the time?
Oh, no! My goods will get wet!
Do you think the road will get blocked off if it snows?
I... I can't see the sun!
Care to browse through some specialties? I have lots of high-quality items.
Oh, my! Look at the snow!
What? The sun is gone? This must be the work of a demon!
Take a look at my wares! Or don't...
I have lots of great items at affordable prices!
We're able to do business here in this dangerous place, thanks to the Resistance Guard.
Get away! I hate how bugs are attracted to the light.
Now I'll have less customers since it's raining. What to do...?
I can't believe I have to do business in this weather. Oh, dear!
Do you see that? The sky got dark!
You think that weapon could pierce the thick leather of the orcs?
Don't you have any other armor? Don't tell me you're going to keep wearing that.
The Flame Watcher? That's a great title!
I-I have nothing more to sell. Please let me go.
I can tell you're a rookie, even from far away. You should train some more and come back when you're ready.
Lots of adventurers have passed by, but I've never seen an Amitoi that's better than yours.
Check if you have all the consumables you need before entering a dungeon.
I was almost ambushed by goblins on my way here today. The Resistance saved me.
Ugh. It's so dark. I should go home.
It rains too often around here.
Don't the goblins ever get cold?
That weapon of yours looks great on you.
Starlight Collector? If you like stars, you should hang around the Observatory!
You don't have to buy anything. Please, just go...
^<c=@MK_D_Dialogue>{gva_PcName}^</c>? What's a celebrity doing here at the Observatory?
What's the name of that cute doll that's following you around?
Take a look at the village specialties! We have lots of high-quality leather.
The village is so busy these days. It's great for business.
Kastleton is the best place to live!
The rain is going to ruin business for the day!
A warm drink at the inn is perfect on a cold day like this!
Don't you need a stronger weapon? You should go speak to the Equipment Merchant.
The Equipment Merchant is an honest fellow. Go visit if you ever need new clothes.
I heard the Golden Rye Pastures are safe now. It's all thanks to you.
Lobsters were a common thing to eat before the ocean got polluted. Now only peculiar people like you are after them.
Your Contract Coin Pouch looks pretty heavy! Don't you know Coins are meant to be used, not collected?
Where did you get that fascinating Amitoi?
You've got to buy some of our village specialty wine! You won't find prices like this anywhere else.
I'll give you a special discount. Come in! Come in!
Oh, would you look at the time?
Did you know? When it rains too much, wine loses its flavor.
Winter in the desert is harsh. You should prepare yourself.
I'm sure the gods are angry at us! You should pray, too!
I can't believe you crossed the desert in those tattered clothes! There's a talented Armor Crafter in Vienta, you know.
If you want to travel through Stonegard, you'll need better weapons. Why don't you get yourself some new equipment?
That's a rare Amitoi that money just can't buy. Where did you get it?
You came back alive from the Sandworm Lair? You're a monster!
If you don't get hot easily, it must be easy for you to travel through the desert.
Oh! A special customer! What brings you to Vienta, ^<c=@MK_D_Dialogue>{gva_PcName}^</c>?
A special customer from the {gva_PcGuildName} guild! Take all the time you need.
It doesn't matter how well my business does. After paying taxes, I can barely feed myself.
You should go to the retail shop if you want to buy items. We only take bulk orders here.
If you need food, there's a merchant who makes them.
Oh, no! This isn't supposed to get wet!
The snow is inconvenient for us, but the children love it.
Wasn't it daytime just now? Is this a dream?
You look like an adventurer. Don't you need a better weapon?
Why don't you buy new armor while you're in the castle? The desert monsters are terrifying, you know.
Your Amitoi looks exhausted. I don't think it's faring well in the desert.
Did you come all the way here to the castle to cause trouble again?
If you're not in a guild, you can't deal with the Guild Merchant. You know that, right?
Please tell the lord to have mercy on the merchants.
Even if I do business all day, I have nothing left after taxes! The lord around here has no mercy...
This is the center of all trade in Stonegard! There's nothing you can't find here.
Look at the time! I should take a break.
I'm sure the snow will melt before you know it. Don't worry.
Look at the sky! What could be happening?
Don't you need a better weapon? That weapon won't get you too far.
The more Amitoi you have, the better. How many do you have?
I made eye contact with ^<c=@MK_D_Dialogue>{gva_PcName}^</c>! Today must be my lucky day!
Wh-what? I'm going to call the guard!
If you're friends with the Pirate King, you're no ordinary customer.
You killed that many demons? I can't believe you defeated those terrifying creatures. You must be quite talented.
Aren't you from the {gva_PcGuildName} guild? Oh, you're a very special customer!
The lord is gracious! Now all the merchants can rest easy.
This area used to prosper because of all the lumber exports.
It gets cold very quickly at night, so the merchants go home since there are no customers anyway.
I should call it a day.
Everything is going to get wet! No!
I just can't believe it's snowing!
Did I doze off? How did the sun set already?
Have you visited the Equipment Merchant? Your armor will be torn up by the lycans' claws in an instant.
I used to sell weapons for a while, but I've never seen one like yours before.
There are strong Amitoi and weak Amitoi. Didn't you know that?
Of course, I recognize you, ^<c=@MK_D_Dialogue>{gva_PcName}^</c>. Is there anything you need in Canina Village?
Based on your title, I can tell you've defeated quite a few of those conniving lycans!
Why do the guards allow a murderer to roam free in the village? Think about the children, at least!
Is that an Amitoi? It looks much stronger than the other Amitoi I've seen.
These days, I hardly get to see items that are luxurious enough to satisfy me.
Dinner better be prepared exactly as I instructed.
Snow? I should have ridden the carriage.
I wouldn't have come out if I knew it would rain.
Why is it raining all of a sudden?
Improving the lives of commoners can help the village to prosper. I always keep that in mind.
Would you like to hear the history of our family?
Late salon gatherings are difficult to attend.
I should have them take care of the roof so that the snow doesn't pile up.
I should have brought an umbrella...
The climate of Stonegard is dry. It's a scorching desert, after all.
I'm always rooting for the Resistance.
It's finally cooling down a bit.
I hope the rain cools off the heat.
I need to take a break in the shade.
Kastleton has become much livelier, but many people are still anxious.
I usually send someone else for errands at the port to avoid its fishy smell.
The village economy has become more prosperous thanks to the Resistance.
I'm done for today. I'll head home now.
The weather calls for clothing with fine fur.
Oh, no... It'll get humid in the library.
It suddenly got dark... I'm sure this is the work of the gods.
What? You killed a fellow member of the Resistance?
I heard the Blackhowl Plains are a dangerous place. You must be very strong.
Lobster Maniac? You have peculiar taste, don't you?
I heard there are many benefits of joining a guild.
Which guild did you join? I'm so curious.
Oh! I've never seen that Amitoi before.
^<c=@MK_D_Dialogue>{gva_PcName}^</c>? I wasn't expecting to meet someone famous today!
If you need anything, go visit the workshop or market.
Ugh... My skin hasn't been in good condition lately.
Public order is still much better compared to before.
I knew it. The sky had me worried.
I'm sure this rain will pass soon.
People like you should be locked up in the underground prison with the monsters.
Where did you find such a fine Amitoi? My child would love to have one like that.
It's an honor to be acquainted with someone famous as you.
Judging from your clothes, you must be the modest sort.
The castle is so lively these days, all thanks to the gracious lord.
Even though we're surrounded by the desert, our village has no shortage of water. We owe the wizards for that.
The wine of Vienta is pretty good.
I should tell them to keep the light on for the children.
I hope the sand dust settles soon.
Criminals should be arrested on the spot.
I heard there are lots of interesting monsters in the Moonlight Desert. Is that true?
If you're not a member of a guild, don't you miss out on a lot of stuff?
What's the name of your cute Amitoi?
Everyone in Vienta Village respects you, ^<c=@MK_D_Dialogue>{gva_PcName}^</c>.
You must be part of the {gva_PcGuildName} guild that defends Stonegard Castle. Please take good care of Vienta Village.
How do they expect us to pay these taxes? I'll have to sell everything I have...
With so many adventurers coming here these days, my potions have been selling like hot cakes.
I like how I get to travel to various villages, thanks to the nature of my job.
The stars must be aligned when you're in the business of buying and selling. You can't just put something out and expect to turn a profit.
I'd better organize the ledger in bed.
It's snowing again? I hope the carriage doesn't slip on the road.
A diligent merchant doesn't rest even in heavy rain.
I used to think Laslan was done for... But it turns out there's no other place like it.
The life of a peddler is a lonely one.
The night air feels so refreshing.
Oh, I might have to expect lots of traffic.
Darn. All my stuff is going to get wet.
You might wonder what we could possibly sell in the desert. But it's actually chock-full of endless possibilities for us merchants.
The sand is such a nuisance. Ugh, it's coarse and rough and irritating.
Maybe I should go rest now.
I can't hold business because of the snow.
I'm glad it's raining. It'll cool down the scorching weather.
War is the absolute worst. But what can we do about it?
Snow? I definitely can't go out tonight.
Even the weather is against me...
The sky is red? The gods must be angry!
Should I feel lucky to not have starved to death yet?
Well, we're still alive, thanks to the Resistance.
I'm grateful to the Resistance's adventurers.
When is the rain going to stop?
Oh, my... What happened to the sky?
Whatever... I'm just trudging along, day by day...
Everything was great before the war. The Arkeum Legion is to blame for everything that's gone wrong...
I hope things get better before I die.
I hope we all survive through the night...
At least we can drink some water.
Do you make a lot of money if you're in the Resistance?
What's the point of there being lots of shops in the market? People like us can't afford anything.
I'll curse the names of those who started the war until the day I die.
It'll be terrible if it gets any colder.
My child's clothes will get wet again. They have nothing else to wear...
Be careful out there. There are a million things you can trip over near the ship.
Let's call it a day. Now it's time to drink!
Why is it snowing all of a sudden? I should just go home.
I should cover everything up with tarp and take a break.
L-look over there! That's definitely a bad sign!
Seems like there are more travelers here now, huh? That's good news.
If you're from an island, did you come here on a ship?
Ships require constant maintenance to keep afloat.
Did you hear DaVinci invented navigation technology using magic? I hear that ships can travel to different continents in a jiffy now!
We take good care of our cargo, but we always seem to miss something when we have big shipments.
Aren't you curious about what lies beyond the ocean?
The sun sets so fast these days. I can barely get any work done.
Snow? Again? But I just cleared it away!
I should clean the deck while it's raining.
The gods are definitely angry at us!
Huh? Do you have business with me?
Just ask me if you have any questions!
It's raining again! I'm sick and tired of this.
You should pray until the sun comes back!
What's the most famous thing here?
I'm so tired. I should go back.
You should stay out of the rain.
Oh, my... It looks like everything is covered in blood!
I can't believe that I'm really here in Laslan. I thought it was completely reduced to ash.
I didn't even do anything and it's already nighttime.
I heard Laslan is famous for the snow...
The weather is awful... I wouldn't be here if it weren't for the wine.
Touring might be better when it's cooler at night.
How is it snowing in the desert?
Phew. It's better now that it's raining.
Aren't all fellow travelers friends? It's nice to meet you.
I like how quiet this village is at night.
I hope the air smells nice and fresh after the rain.
I heard the Akidu orcs are very strong. You must be quite skilled.
So, you're the Reaper that all werewolves fear.
We free spirits are just fine without a guild.
It must be nice to have such a strong Amitoi with you.
Everyone in my hometown has heard about you, ^<c=@MK_D_Dialogue>{gva_PcName}^</c>.
Are you on a long journey? Your clothes look worn out.
Some Resistance soldiers were running toward Grayclaw Forest just now. Is something happening?
Sorry, but I'm working right now. Please talk to someone else if you need help.
There's no end to all this work...
It's already this late? I still have much to do...
Snow or not, the work's gotta be done.
It's good to be busy, but only if you're getting paid.
I'm glad I had a hearty meal before coming.
Maybe I'll get a glass of mead after work.
It's easy to get hurt while working out in the cold, so you should always be careful.
They should let us wear raincoats while working! Look at how messy I've gotten.
Is it nighttime? That means I can go home!
If you don't take breaks from time to time, you could faint from heatstroke.
I feel dizzy after working in the sun all day.
I'm busy. We can talk later.
It's time to calculate the daily wages.
It's going to get cold pretty soon.
Darn! My clothes are going to get wet!
Did I doze off? I swear it was daytime just a minute ago!

When you work at the port, your skin gets all salty.
The wine produced in Vienta is popular overseas, too!
I haven't seen you before. Where are you from?
Huh? It smells fishy? Well, obviously! We're at a port!
Stand back if you're not going to help.
Darn this rain! We're going to be delayed again.
No wonder. My back has been aching.
No wonder. My joints have been aching.
What's going on? Why is it dark all of a sudden?
A sudden solar eclipse? This can't be a good sign.
Why is it raining all of a sudden...?!
Life isn't all that bad these days. It's all thanks to the Resistance.
Time sure flies. I can't believe how long it's been since the Arkeum Legion's invasion...
I wonder if the kids got home safely...
It'll be hard to walk around once the snow piles up...
When it rains, my whole body aches...

It must be good to be young. They have so much energy, even in this heat.
Sometimes, I just want to sit outside and do nothing.
Never thought I'd live to see this...
The shade is the best on a hot day.
I'm just grateful for everything these days. Thanks to DaVinci and the Resistance, I have things to be grateful for.
Is it your first time here? I dare you to find a better place to live!
I'll watch the sunset before going home.
I'm going to sweep up the snow in front of my house.
Did I close the window at home?
Ahh! I don't have anything! I swear!
The Conqueror of Wolves? You did something wonderful for us all. Thank you.
You shouldn't go around telling secrets. You'll understand when you're older.
You're famous, aren't you? How are you faring these days?
Guild members help each other out, right? Good for you.
This is just a farm. It's nothing special. I just hope for a good harvest in the fall.
The sun has to be hot for the grain to ripen properly.
You're the one who protected the rye fields? Oh, thank you so much.
The night brings out all the mosquitos and bugs.
I should sweep up the snow.
Did you come to buy our village's wine? I feel like there are more travelers visiting these days.
Every day is so hot nowadays.
Oh, my knees. It's too steep.
Snow? I never thought I'd live to see this.
I hope to collect a lot of rainwater.
Oh! I don't have a penny on me!
Wow, you're amazing. You're in the Resistance's top three?
I hear that joining a guild is all the rage these days.
You're in the guild that owns the castle, right? Please take good care of our village.
The taxes these days... Tsk tsk... Huh? Oh, it's nothing.
You can't ignore the heat just because you're young. You'll be sorry if you do!
Everyone here is a merchant. That's why the living conditions are much better here than in other villages.
I heard that this oasis was created by a certain archwizard.
I can't believe this is happening.
I should clean up everything outside the tent.
You're up there in the ranks? You must be quite talented.
You should always be a member of a guild. Then, you get to help your fellow members and be helped by them in return.
The Pirate King is just a legend. I don't know why the young people are so crazy about it.
Some of the youngsters think the Werewolf is just an old legend. Little do they know it's lurking around in that forest.
Wait... Did you hear that wolf's howl? If you didn't, then never mind...
I should go back before it gets dark.
I wonder if it'll pile up.
The trees are going to grow up nice and tall.
Agh! I don't have any money!
A ranker? You must be very strong...
I heard you taught those lycans a lesson! Thanks a lot. We're safe because of you.
I love talking to young people.
My shoulders are a little stiff today...
In my time, I was pretty strong myself.
The snow reminds me of my childhood...
When it rains, my knees hurt and it's hard to get around.
When the sky is like this, weird things happen.
Be careful not to get caught in the storm.
That's one hell of a weapon. My husband had a weapon shop when he was young.
There's a lot of talk about you in the village. You're so young and so skilled.
There's a lot of talk about you in the village. You're so impressive.
I wish I could get my granddaughter an Amitoi...
The Swamp of Silence is home to a monster even more dangerous than the ferocious sharks.
Looking for the best techs in Talandre? Everyone's great. Just ask.
You know the saying, imitation is the mother of creation, right? That's how a lot of technology came to be.
Many technicians are taking on the challenge of developing ways to light up the darkness.
I wonder if it's snowing where my son is.
I'm building a device to predict how much rain will fall.
At some point in your life, a solar eclipse shouldn't surprise you.
If only there was a technology that could predict heavy rain...
Can you show me your equipment? It doesn't look like ordinary equipment to me.
I've heard my son talk about you. He said you were amazing.
I'm not interested in fighting, but I've heard your name before.
Amitoi never cease to amaze me.
You have to be able to read the weather to farm properly.
I don't have much to do at my age. Working in the fields is my only pastime.
Farmers still have a lot of work to do at night.
I need to cover everything from getting snowed on.
All of my joints are aching.
When the cursed rain fell ten years ago, I thought we were all done for.
Since the Resistance is working to protect us, I can enjoy farming in peace.
Yikes. I should go home now.
Oh, dear. I hope the fields don't freeze.
The rain is nice and moist.
All the rye will fall down because of the rainstorm!
Good wine comes from good grapes.
The grapes from our village are the best in the world.
The sun has to come out for the grapes to ripen.
Now that the weather is cooler, I should go to bed.
At this rate, I won't be able to pay all the taxes, even if the harvest turns out great.
You should try the apricots before you leave the village.
The harvest continues, and we live without worry.
I'd better get home, so I can work again tomorrow.
The right amount of snow helps with farming.
What's wrong with the sky...? It won't hurt the crops, will it?
I was hoping for some rain, but not this much.
Nice equipment! I can see it even with my bad eyes!
Oh, you've defeated a lot of monsters. Thank you!
Welcome. This place is famous for its apricot jam. You must try it!
My grandson walks around like that Amitoi of yours.
It's a good day for fishing.
What fish will I catch today?
Can I see anything in the dark? Hoho, fishing isn't done with your eyes.
Uh-oh, it's snowing. I'm just going to catch one and go home.
The bite is slow on a rainy day. Even the fish have sore joints.
Oh no, the sky is dark. Even the fish must think it's bedtime.
Who's making it rain like this?
That's a great piece of equipment! I have the same thing... No? My eyes are blurry.
You're famous, aren't you? I'd love to catch you a fresh fish.
You're the famous adventurer. Enjoy fishing and relaxing.
That's an Amitoi, isn't it? I'd love to have one next to me when I'm fishing!
It's harder to see now that it's night...
Be careful not to fall in the snow. You could be seriously injured.
Rain is a blessing to the earth.
Mm? Are we in a solar eclipse right now?
There is a price to pay for changing the weather.
You must be very strong to be carrying all that heavy equipment. Good for you!
Did I finish all my work for today?
The Purelight Tower was built to purify this land of all darkness.
I sense powerful magic! Someone caused this solar eclipse.
Someone is making the rain fall. I can feel the magic flowing.
Hm... Is this artificial rain? Well, as long as it's not cursed...
Many of the wizards here came from Venelux.
The power of darkness is more dangerous because it can spread to other beings.
Young Leon has great potential. He knows how to follow the natural order.
Elter from Venelux and Leon, who was born here, have an unspoken rivalry.
I've researched the Great Sage Tree all my life, but it's still full of mysteries.
In this forest, Passage Ceremonies happen on a regular basis for the elves' souls.
Sigh, I can't see clearly anymore. Is there a magic that gives you better eyesight?
When it rains like this, I can tell that the trees love it.
Someone has used the Eclipse magic. What an amazing power.
This downpour doesn't feel right. It must be caused by magic.
If you're curious, you can come take a proper look. I won't charge you or anything.
The profits just aren't very much these days...
No! All my goods will go bad!
Why is it raining all of a sudden? Is a storm brewing?
Check this out. There are lots of great items other than wine!

I should close up shop now.
You'll be eaten alive with that sort of equipment! You need something much better.
Are you the one everybody wants as their comrade? You're popular, aren't you?

Hahaha! Life is good these days. The lord is so kind to us all.
I think the taxes are too high... There! I said it!
Um... Could you maybe ask the lord to lower the tax rate?

I only sell stuff I'd give to my grandkids.

What's with all the snow? I hope my products don't freeze.

The sky is acting up again. Don't worry. It happens sometimes.
I don't mind the rain, but I can't stand the wind!
Wow, your equipment is really shiny!
You're the one who goes around defeating all the monsters. Thank you.
You're one of the top two members of the Resistance, aren't you? Feel free to look around.
Did you know that every Amitoi has a different personality?
Just take it one step at a time. Better safe than sorry.

It's already been two days since our Abyss Exploration Team entered Syleus's Abyss. Our captain, Mr. Lester, once again emphasized that we should not forget our purpose. As many adventurers lost their lives here, our goal is to acquire and deliver as much information about this place as possible so that many adventurers can avoid danger. <np>And today, we learned some very important information. On the first and second floors of Syleus's Abyss, ^<c=@Codex_ACH_HN>Specters^</c> appear, in numbers equal to the number of dark skulls defeated! For every dark skull destroyed, a Specter takes its place... A hopeless cycle. If this information is shared with future adventurers, can we save more lives? I can only hope.

It's already been a week since we entered Syleus's Abyss. In the meantime, Mason was injured and retreated with Bartz. Captain Lester ordered us to move with extreme caution. The deeper we go, the more we will not be able to retreat easily even when being injured. And after standing firm, we found out additional information. Here on the Abyss's third and fourth floors, ^<c=@Codex_ACH_HN>the fallen armor^</c> can be seen here and there. Thinking that it might be the remains of adventurers who died fighting with monsters here, my colleagues and I gathered the armor and tried to offer a prayer. <np>But then, something like a spirit dwelling in the armor stirred. If the captain hadn't ordered a quick retreat, we could have died while praying. I thought that Mr. Lester, who didn't offer a prayer, was cold-blooded... I guess there is a reason he is the captain. Anyway, this information must be reported to the outside world, so I'm writing it down here.

Exploration of Syleus's Abyss, Day 32. The injured were convoyed above ground. In the meantime, we met a group of amazing adventurers who had come down here, and among them was Bartz, who had brought a load of supplies. How lucky! They decided to help us in our exploration. It's a guild that enjoys risky challenges... Of course, we're thankful, but I was not comfortable when I heard the captain muttering that people like this always go missing in the Abyss. <np>They say that this is the deepest part, but something is wrong. I think that the structure of the Abyss keeps changing. A while back, I found a fragile stone bridge and flowing lava... After a while, I noticed that the shape of the bridge had changed. We need to uncover the ^<c=@Codex_ACH_HN>secret^</c> of the Abyss's structure. Today, I found a bloody note left by someone. Their last words. A morbid reminder of the dangers here.
Thank you for lifting Cornelius's curse.
I was trapped here for so long because of him. But now, at last, I am free...

Oh, even the air feels cold here... I'd never come here if it wasn't for this.
Sometimes you see the purple Undead near the Cenotaph. They are so creepy...
But the merchants must go where they should go.
I heard the most important thing is to activate the Cenotaph. Ya know?
Aren't the Wolves fierce? You'd better be careful.
It's already been ten years since Lord Hobs's son passed away. How time flies...
High-quality Wolf Tails are used for all kinds of things.
You can't just collect Wolf Tails! You have to deliver them, too!
Which delivery post will still have space at the end of today?
An orc on fire! I would never have believed it if I didn't see them with me own eyes!
I heard the Fonos orcs were fighters. What made them dabble in such dangerous sorcery...?
Heading straight to the altar where the Fire Ritual will be held isn't a bad idea.
Just the sight of the shining Starlight Stones makes me glad that I came here. This is all the happiness I need.
Venelux says they don't need it, but luxury goods yield the highest profit margins for merchants like us.
My mom used to tell me that I must have been a goblin in my past life because I love shiny objects. Heheh.
The Watson Merchants are famous for making money. The youngest may be green, but I hear he's got a way with people.
If they buy Lantern Seeds at such a high price, I don't know if they will make any profit.
Have you used a Soulstone before? They're worth the high price tag.
You need World Tree Leaves for your Amitoi to give you recovery magic.
If someone looks the same, doesn't mean their skills haven't grown.
When you're not sure what you need, start with some World Tree Leaves.
Be careful touching the chests left along the coast. There might be vicious crabs hiding inside.
I'm in a particularly good mood today.
I can focus purely on my job as a merchant, thanks to the Wizards in this area. They sure know how to spend!
I've heard there are some incredible high-ranking spells. They say there are some that can control the weather.
Everyone knows plants are weak to fire. You'd be smart to go hunting with allies who use Flame Arrows or flame magic.
As long as I've been selling, I still have a hard time catching onto the bizarre preferences and personalities of the Wizards.
This place used to be called Aelon Hill, and its previous owner, Grand Aelon, is still alive and well - you'll find him by heading a little further north of the tower.
People say Wizards tend to be night owls because they get so carried away with their research, but it's actually because they have to stay alert when the Undead come alive at dark.
Careful, Plantaria monsters near the Purelight Tower don't die easily on rainy days.
If you morph into a goblin type, goblins won't attack you first! Did you know that? Hahaha.
Confident in your abilities? Use a Resistance Contract Scroll to get an Abyssal Contract and enter the Abyss. Two birds, one stone!
At night, the whole area falls quiet, and Specters appear around the Shattered Temple up there, and Dark Rifts are said to form. Oh, it gives me the shivers.
When it rains and the forest is damp... Only a select few know that you can gather Death Cap Mushrooms in the forest.
Greetings, customer! Where are you off to? Whatever you need, take a look!
Orcs above, undead below. It's dangerous, but if you're well prepared you can get good rewards.
When I tell people I do business here, they ask, "What? In such a dangerous place?" However, I think this is probably one of the safest places in Laslan.
The Fonos Clan is known for its cruelty even among orcs. You'd better be fully prepared.
The more dangerous the Territory, the more thoroughly you need to prepare.
Don't go to the Ruins of Turayne at night. It's said the energy of the night makes the undead faster and stronger.
It's raining. Why don't you check your bag one more time? Who knows? You might be running low on something.
I don't mean to rush you, but you should hurry.
Hurry, before the Requiem of Light ends!
It's dangerous here, so it's best to be well prepared!
By the way, you must be really brave to have come all the way to this place.
An adventurer participating in the Requiem of Light. Welcome!
Come, come! Take a close look and choose wisely!
This is one of the most dangerous places in Laslan. You'd better be careful.
Don't you have to be well prepared to claim victory in the contest?
Come, come! See if we have what you need!
A hunter left without preparations earlier. I wonder if they're alright.
You must be getting ready for the Hunting Contest!
You must be participating in the contest!
You never know which Campsite Delivery Chest will fill up first, so deliver fast!
If you need something, just let me know!
They used to give Tokens to contest participants, but not anymore, huh?
You must be here to put out the orcs' flames!
Hurry! You must go and stop the orcs!
If you want to defeat goblins, you need to be well equipped!
Stardust... I might make some money by selling them!
The merchants give nice rewards to people who deliver a lot of seeds. It's a rather clever way of doing business!
I can guarantee this potion's quality!
Anything you need, just let me know. I'm always ready to listen to my customers.
I've carefully selected only the best items. Please, take a look.
The customer is a king? No. The customer is a god. A god!
Come one, come all, before it's all sold out! Buy it quick when you need it!
Over here! The best sundries in all of Laslan!
It's best to stay stocked up on items.
Based on what you're carrying, you must be headed to Fonos Basin. A lot of orcs will be falling today!
Notice! To everyone. Notice! A new. Solisium recording. Has begun. Has begun!
Notice! A record. Is being. Actively recorded. As a. Milestone!
Notice! Notice! The Milestone. Is almost complete. Almost complete!
Notice! Notice! Recording of a. New history. Has begun. Please check. The Milestone!
Notice! Notice! Please take part. In recording the. Historical record. Please take part!
Notice! Notice! The historical record. Is almost complete. Almost complete!
Attention! Attention! A new story. Has begun. The Milestone. Has begun!
Attention! This is! A chance. To make a name. For yourself. In history!
Attention! Attention! A new page. In history. Is almost complete! Almost complete!
Focus! This is! A chance. To make a name. For yourself. In history! The Milestone. Has begun!
Notice! Recording. Milestone. Activity. Success! Recording. Success!
Notice! Recording. Final. Milestone. Record. Please read. With interest!
Attention! Attention! A new. Story. Is about to! Unfold!
Attention! Attention! Your active role. Is being recorded. In history! Please take part!
Attention! Attention! The story. Is ending. Please check! The final. Milestone record! Please check!
Attention! Attention! A new. Milestone. Is now. Open! Now open!
Attention! Attention! There is. A Milestone. Being actively recorded. Please check!
Attention! Attention! A Milestone. Is. Almost complete! Almost complete! Please check!
Do you want to make your skills stronger? This is the right place.
You can use your Parchment Scrolls here.
You absolutely need to grow skills. It's a must.
It is really important to grow your skills.
Is there anything else you'd like to see?
Look around carefully and you'll know what you need.
Researching skills is very intense work.
Use your hard-earned parchment to learn various skills.
The harder it is to find, the more effective it'll be. That, I can assure!
I'm glad you came. Learning helps to overcome your limits!
Oh, brother! Why is your bag so heavy?
Have you tried using the Storage? It's very convenient!
Yawwwn. I'm the Storage keeper of Kastleton, a town of rich history and culture!
The Storage is always open, rain or shine.
Your bag looks a little bit heavy there. Maybe get it organized first?
I've been working at the Starlight Observatory Ruins Storage for a long time, years now!
Haaah... I wasn't really asleep... So, what do you need?
Even if it's raining and pouring, shining objects are easy to spot.
Hey! You over there! Are you having trouble using the Storage?
Let's get your stuff organized. Isn't your bag heavy?
Ugh... It's pretty late, middle of the night even! What could you possibly need?
I'll be here safeguarding the Storage, no matter what it takes!
I'll keep your things safe, so you can rest easy!
You can retrieve things you left here in any town! Just find the Storage Manager!
You sure you organized your bag?
Be careful out there, you're an important customer to me!
Leaving already? Take care now. It's my pleasure serving you.
Come back anytime! I'll be here waiting.
Oh, my favorite customer! Did you forget to leave something with me?
Anything you don't absolutely need while hunting, leave it here with me!
My favorite customer is back. Did you forget something important?
A light bag is best when you're going on an adventure.
You're back again? Did you forget something?
Did you have more stuff to put in Storage? I had a feeling...
You're back again? Have you got more stuff to put in Storage?
Oh, you're back again so soon! When heading out on an adventure, packing light is a good idea.
Are you going to take all those materials with you?
If you're not sure how to organize your stuff, just let me know!
Is your Storage feeling a bit too small? Want to know how to expand it?
What's all that stuff in your bag? We can even help take your stuff to the crafters.
There's no strategic benefit to having a heavy bag!
I swear I'm not just saying this to make more money... But are you sure your Storage is big enough?
If you're not sure what to leave with me, just ask. I'll just pick out your materials and keep them for you.
Are you bad at organizing? Just say the word, and I'll arrange everything in order of rarity.
It's great to have as many materials as possible, but there's no need to lug them all around with you!
There's no need to overthink it. Just leave it here, and if you need it later, just come back and get it.
Is your Storage full already? Just say the word and we'll expand it for you!
Crafting or dissolving... There's plenty of ways to get all your stuff nice and organized!
Don't worry about your materials so much. Just put them in Storage!
You got some neat-lookin' stuff here, brother. I'm havin' fun just looking after it!
Our service can't be beat! You have absolutely nothing to lose!
This is the safest Storage in the world!
Hoho! Did you come to see me?
I want to give you a big discount, too, friend! But I can't...
Hello there! Planning on going hunting?
It's good you're here! Leave your baggage with me and you can come and go as you please!
Sometimes I envy how free you adventurers are!
It's good to meet you, brother! We'll be seeing a lot of each other from now on.
Your belongings are safe and sound, as usual!
Don't even worry about the Storage! No matter what happens, I'll be sure to protect it!
Looking for a weapon to fight Immorti? You've come to the right place.
I see you've heard the rumors. Every weapon I make is exceptional.
It's time for the undead to grow stronger. You need a weapon you can rely on at a time like this.
What appalling weather. Are you here because you need a weapon?
We'll meet again if destiny wills it.
There is no way of knowing when death will come. Use your time wisely.
Toiho, friend! If you need a weapon you can count on, you've come to the right place!
What kind of weapon do you need, my friend?
I know the entire crafting process. Just leave it to me.
It's our duty as crafters to make weapons for adventurers.
