The Wildkin have been greatly increasing in number lately, disrupting the natural environment in certain areas. This is a request to exterminate Wildkin to restore the biome. You will be compensated by the Tree of Life Society.

The damage caused by Constructs like the Golems and Harshcrows is becoming more serious. Destroy these aberrations to keep the situation from getting worse. You will be rewarded for aiding the Allied Resistance Forces.

Demon sightings have increased significantly of late, and they are causing a great deal of harm to pilgrims and adventurers. Get rid of Demons to prevent further casualties. You will be rewarded for aiding the Lightbringer Society.

There has been a rapid increase in the number of destructive incidents caused by Undead. Would a battle-hardened warrior please help clear them out? The Allied Resistance Forces will certainly repay those who exterminate Undead.

Local Wildkin have been attacking villagers and their livestock, and their population is still growing. We are requesting help in hunting them to keep their numbers under control. The Solisium Hunting Union will generously compensate those who off any Wildkin.
Cases of violent bandits killing civilians are on the rise. The Allied Resistance Forces will reward anyone who can eliminate this threat.

We are seeking courageous warriors to join us in putting a stop to the ruthless killing of innocents committed by the Arkeum Legion and other bandits. Please eliminate these cruel evildoers. You will be rewarded for aiding the Allied Resistance Forces.

The destruction of the ecosystem has been exacerbated due to the abnormal increase in the number of Wildkin. We need to defend nature against their unnatural growth. You will be rewarded for aiding the Tree of Life Society.

The ecosystem's balance is collapsing due to the unusual increase in Wildkin. This is a request to stomp out Wildkin monsters in order to maintain the natural ecosystem. You will be rewarded for aiding the Tree of Life Society.

Recently, the mana consumption of Undead has exploded, causing all our spells and devices to malfunction. Please eliminate the Undead to normalize the flows of mana. You will be rewarded for aiding the Lightbringer Society.
Hunt down all creatures, regardless of species, that threaten the virtuous people of this world.

According to recent intel, demons are planning to imbue wild animals and plants with dark powers and lead them in an attack on the human villages. Exterminate Demons and Wildkin to prevent any further damage. You will be rewarded for aiding Venelux.

Recently, Undead have been contaminating the surrounding flora and fauna, causing a rapid increase in monstrous Wildkin. Please defeat the Wildkin and Undead to stop the situation from getting worse. Venelux will reward you.

There is a concerning rise in reports of missing people in the deserts and forests. We determined these disappearances are the work of Humanoid raiders, with the help of evil wild animals and plants. Defeat these criminals and their Wildkin allies. You will be rewarded for aiding the Solisium Adventurers Association.

There has been a strange phenomenon of wild animals and plants rapidly turning into monsters and attacking Resistance fortresses. It turns out this is a plot by criminals who are working with Arkeum. Defeat the raiders and Wildkin, and you will be rewarded for aiding the Allied Resistance Forces.

Wildkin, led by Temitrans and the Kowazan Clan, are terrorizing the peddlers and travelers on the roads connecting the desert and forest. Defeat these Wildkin and make the roads safe again. You will be rewarded for aiding the Stonegard Traders' Guild.

The dispute between the Demons and local Humanoid criminals has grown increasingly tense, and the innocent Trust Union goblins nearby have been caught in the crossfire. If someone were to put and end to their violent dispute, they would be well rewarded by the Steel Trust Union.
Demons and Constructs are harassing the goblins of the Steel Trust Union. The Steel Trust Union will pay to those who get rid of them.

A few days ago, after a deep purple fog rolled in, the soulless undead and golems began to run wild. Please curb the Undead and Constructs before they become too powerful to suppress. You will be rewarded for aiding Venelux.
Demons and the undead are everywhere. Please defeat the Undead and Demons before they cause any further damage. You will be rewarded by Venelux.

Raiders have begun attacking civilians alongside Undead forces. I don't know if it's a mere coincidence or a well-executed plan, but there have been many casualties. Please protect our Resistance allies by eliminating both factions. You will be rewarded for aiding the Allied Resistance Forces.

The Arkeum Legion and their allies have begun attacking the Resistance on multiple fronts. As our casualties mount, we have to put an end to their slaughter by eliminating the Arkeum's allies. You will be rewarded for aiding the Allied Resistance Forces.

Resistance forces sent to take care of bandits have encountered Undead and need reinforcements. Help push back against the enemy forces and Undead. You will be rewarded for aiding the Allied Resistance Forces.

Arkeum's allies and Wildkin are upsetting the peace, and causing trouble for the innocent people of Solisium. Defeat these threats and put an end to their chaos. The Allied Resistance Forces will reward you.
There are many who wish to destroy Solisium, some mortal, some immortal. Push back against Arkeum's allies, both Demonic and Humanoid, who are wreaking chaos in Solisium. Venelux will reward you.

The recent magic instability is causing an increasing number of mutants. An investigation team from Venelux is researching this phenomenon, but the mutant monsters make it too dangerous to proceed. Please defeat the mutated Wildkin that are hampering our efforts. Venelux will reward you.

Our world has no shortage of mysteries. Amidst unseen threats, some forces are trying to take on the powers of Diabolica. Stop the Demons trying to open the door to Diabolica and the violent Wildkin that are affected by their power. Venelux will reward those who come to our aid.

Recently, an abnormal mana phenomenon has spread, turning the natural unnatural, and the dead undead. Please defeat these Wildkin and Undead aberrations that threaten the laws of nature. Venelux will reward those who come to our aid.
The natural biome is in danger. Please eliminate Arkeum's allies and the Wildkin working with them before they can cause more harm to the environment. Venelux will reward those who come to our aid.

Solisium's peddlers are growing fearful due to the recent attacks by Wildkin and bandits. Help us maintain the safety of our brave traders in the region by eliminating these looming threats. You will be rewarded for aiding the Solisium Merchants Association.

We mortals are humbled before nature's might, but we must respond to its threats and protect our people. Please defeat the violent Wildkin that are endangering local fauna and people. The Lightbringer Society has prepared a reward.

Wildkin and Demons are attacking Venelux wizards seeking to study the area and its mana. Eliminate these threats so our allies can complete their research. Guilds that come to their aid will be rewarded.
We're having a hard time transporting our cargo on time as Demons and Wildkin keep attacking us. Eliminate these foes, and the Solisium Merchants Association will be in your debt.

There have been frequent reports lately of tourists in Solisium being attacked by Arkeum's allies and mutant wildlife. The Allied Resistance Forces are urging the active support of the Resistance to maintain the security of Solisium.

Damage caused by lost Constructs and angry Wildkin is on the rise. It's extremely important to put an end to this situation before it gets out of hand. If your guild can help us, the Allied Resistance Forces will reward you.

^<imgf=IMG_Help_Dot_Markup_01> Private Housing is a system where you arrange the furniture you've obtained to decorate your own home.
^<imgf=IMG_Help_Dot_Markup_01> Players can purchase and own a house in the world, and can set it so other players can visit their home.

^<imgf=IMG_Help_Dot_Markup_01> Types of Houses
^<imgf=IMG_Help_Arrow_Markup_01> Houses are located in various places throughout the world and are classified according to the following criteria.
^<imgf=IMG_Help_Arrow_Markup_01> Affiliated Dominion: Classified by the dominion the house belongs to. To purchase a house in a specific dominion, you need the ^<imgf=IMG_Housing_PurchaseHouse> "Housing Purchase Permit" item for that dominion.
^<imgf=IMG_Help_Arrow_Markup_01> Size: Classified by scale as "^<imgf=IMG_Housing_Door_kLarge> Large," "^<imgf=IMG_Housing_Door_kMiddle > Medium," "^<imgf=IMG_Housing_Door_kSmall> Small," or "^<imgf=IMG_Housing_Door_kBase> Basement."
^<imgf=IMG_Help_Arrow_Markup_01> Each house has its own separate storage. To place furniture in a house, the furniture must first be moved to the "House Storage."
^<imgf=IMG_Help_Arrow_Markup_01> The maximum storage size varies depending on the house size.

^<imgf=IMG_Help_Dot_Markup_01> House Ownership
^<imgf=IMG_Help_Arrow_Markup_01> If you meet the purchase conditions for a house, you can buy a new one.
^<imgf=IMG_Help_Arrow_Markup_01> A player can own up to 4 houses in the world, and one of them can be set as the "Main House."
^<imgf=IMG_Help_Arrow_Markup_01> The house set as the "Main House" can be visited by other players.

^<imgf=IMG_Help_Dot_Markup_01> Furniture Value
^<imgf=IMG_Help_Arrow_Markup_01> All ^<imgf=IMG_Housing_Furniture> furniture has its own unique "Value."

^<imgf=IMG_Help_Dot_Markup_01> House Rating
^<imgf=IMG_Help_Arrow_Markup_01> The ^<imgf=IMG_Housing_HousePower> House Rating is determined by the total value of furniture stored in that house's ^<imgf=IMG_Housing_Storage> "storage".
^<imgf=IMG_Help_Arrow_Markup_01> Each house has a set limit, within its storage capacity, for how many pieces can count toward the House Rating.
^<imgf=IMG_Help_Arrow_Markup_01> The system sums the values of the highest-value furniture in storage to calculate the "House Rating".

^<imgf=IMG_Help_Dot_Markup_01> Primary House Rating
^<imgf=IMG_Help_Arrow_Markup_01> If you own multiple houses within the same dominion, the house with the highest House Rating becomes the "Primary House Rating."
^<imgf=IMG_Help_Arrow_Markup_01> This value affects your eligibility to purchase larger houses within that dominion.

^<imgf=IMG_Help_Dot_Markup_01> Total House Rating
^<imgf=IMG_Help_Arrow_Markup_01> The total sum of the House Rating of all houses you own.
^<imgf=IMG_Help_Arrow_Markup_01> "Total House Rating" is displayed on your Character Card, and you can toggle its visibility in the card settings.

^<imgf=IMG_Help_Dot_Markup_01> When interacting with a house door in the world, you can perform the following actions.
^<imgf=IMG_Help_Arrow_Markup_01> Visit My House: Enter the house you own at that location.
^<imgf=IMG_Help_Arrow_Markup_01> Visit Vacant House: Enter an unowned house to check its interior layout.
^<imgf=IMG_Help_Arrow_Markup_01> Purchase House: Purchase a house that is in the "Vacant" state.
^<imgf=IMG_Help_Arrow_Markup_01> Move House: Remove your current house and purchase a new one. All furniture stored in the previous house's storage will be moved to the new house's storage.

^<imgf=IMG_Help_Dot_Markup_01> Through another player's Character Card, you can enter that player's "Main House."
^<imgf=IMG_Help_Dot_Markup_01> If the player has hidden it on their card or restricted visits for their house, you will not be able to visit.

^<imgf=IMG_Help_Dot_Markup_01> Manage My House
^<imgf=IMG_Help_Arrow_Markup_01> View House Information: Displays a list of houses you own and lets you check the each House Rating.
^<imgf=IMG_Help_Arrow_Markup_01> Change Main House: You can set one of your owned houses as the "Main House."
^<imgf=IMG_Help_Arrow_Markup_01> Visitor Settings: You can set the conditions for players allowed to visit your Main House.
^<imgf=IMG_Help_Arrow_Markup_01> Any player who meets at least one of the set conditions can visit.
^<imgf=IMG_Help_Arrow_Markup_01> Achievement Rewards: Depending on your "Total House Rating", you can unlock the right to purchase certain houses or obtain additional rewards.

^<imgf=IMG_Help_Dot_Markup_01> Manage Storage
^<imgf=IMG_Help_Arrow_Markup_01> You can move furniture from your "Miscellaneous Inventory" to the "House Storage" of a chosen house for placement.
^<imgf=IMG_Help_Arrow_Markup_01> Only furniture stored in a house's "House Storage" can be placed in that house.
^<imgf=IMG_Help_Arrow_Markup_01> ^<c=@UI_TXT_Red_Disable>Furniture moved into "House Storage" cannot be moved back to your inventory.^</c>
^<imgf=IMG_Help_Arrow_Markup_01> To transfer furniture from one "House Storage" to another, you need a "^<imgf=IMG_Housing_MoveFurniture> Furniture Transfer Permit."

^<imgf=IMG_Help_Dot_Markup_01> This feature allows you to place furniture in the house you are currently in.
^<imgf=IMG_Help_Dot_Markup_01> In Placement mode, you can only place furniture that has been stored in that house's storage.
^<imgf=IMG_Help_Dot_Markup_01> In addition to placing furniture, you can change the wallpaper and flooring.

^<imgf=IMG_Help_Dot_Markup_01> This system allows you to record and see the various activities and achievements you've made while playing the game.
^<imgf=IMG_Help_Dot_Markup_01> Complete achievements across combat, exploration, and lifestyle activities to earn rewards.
^<imgf=IMG_Help_Dot_Markup_01> Achievement Points are earned automatically when an achievement is completed. Press [Claim] to receive item rewards.
^<imgf=IMG_Help_Arrow_Markup_01> Your Achievement Points can be displayed on your card.
^<imgf=IMG_Help_Dot_Markup_01> You'll receive a special title and rewards upon completing certain achievements.

Navius, a priest of Sylaveth who witnessed the birth of Rex Chimaerus, firmly believed he could create an even more terrible and powerful monstrosity. Defying Elder Belluatan's orders, he infused the sealed temple with horrific power through endless slaughter. The sealed sanctuary's interior was shrouded in the burning magic of curses, while virulent poison that could melt even bone seeped into every crack in the walls and altars. From that abyss, maddened roars echoed endlessly. When the temple finally opened, all that remained was a horrific beast no being could control—one that sought to melt and burn everything, just as it had suffered.

At the darkest, most secret place, a coronation unfolded amid an ominous flash. The subterranean minions sensed at once that their monarch had grown even stronger. Offering as sacrifice those who dared set foot upon her land to build her empire, the queen ant finally absorbed the fragment of the power that had created her, and after a madness-soaked purge, Lyxara at last became the eternal ruler of the underworld.

When the story of Baazul from a Venelux restaurant spread, it became a fad for wizards to transform themselves into Baazul on their way back from work. The most popular color choice for their sheep was the spectacular rainbow jelly color.

A chef of a Venelux restaurant made this Baazul for his children, as a way to say sorry to them for not spending enough time with them because of his work. The sheep was his children's favorite animal, and the children enjoyed the delicious jelly. People were deeply touched by this lovely story, and wizards even created the Baazul morph spell to celebrate the chef's beautiful masterpiece.

Higher tiers of this species can glow increasingly brighter. They can swim in lava, making them a Mystic Beast with no natural predators. They are extremely difficult to capture.

Once a righteous thief who stole from the rich to give to poor goblins, this goblin began to change as his thieving ways became second nature. Greed gradually took hold. He started hoarding the stolen gold for himself, never letting it out of his grasp. Over time, his entire body turned golden, gleaming so brightly that he shone even in the dead of night. Because of this, he was easily spotted during his heists and quickly lost everything. But strangely enough, he didn't mind - in fact, he found his sparkling so stylish that he ended up happier than ever.

Creatures that live in herds within the forests and fields of Laslan. It is said that even professional hunters refrain from hunting deer around Kastleton where there is a legend about a divine beast that takes on such a form. One can naturally blend into field environments when shapeshifted into a fawn but must be wary of potential attacks from predators at the same time.

Chestaceans use the advanced hunting technique of attracting humans or animals with mimicry before attacking. While their natural shells often provide adequate defense, they constantly search for something harder to protect their bodies. As such, these creatures compete fiercely with one another to get the most expensive-looking chest when cargo washes up from shipwrecks on Windhill Shores.

These are a type of dog commonly found on rural farms in Laslan. Their drooping ears and stiff tails melt the heart. After being tamed, they will show unyielding affection and loyalty toward their owners. They often enjoy long walks and delicious snacks. Shapeshifting into a dog can ease the wariness of those around you.

Cats are, by nature, small solitary predators that originally inhabited the wilds of Trutizan. However, due to their natural cuteness, laid-back nature, and ability to catch mice, they became a favorite pet of sailors and farmers. As such, they have spread around the world after being used on ships to protect supplies. Cats are now an object of affection in every single known country.

Sheep come from northern Solisium and Trutizan and have long been raised as livestock for its warm fleece. Sheep from colder plateau regions tend to have increasingly thicker coats. They are mainly raised as grazing animals and are allowed to roam vast fields. Cooperation between a shepherd and their sheepdogs is essential in order to protect these animals from predators.

Large creatures originally from the Grasia region that are used for transportation in the desert regions. Camels have one or two humps that are used to store water. They have large split-hooved feet that enable them to walk freely on sand and thus are often found in the deserts of Stonegard.

While the Young Mage Academy supported by Venelux teaches various types of magic, morph magic is the most popular. One of the first things they teach you in the basic morph classes is how to perform the Oremong Shapeshift, and it is said that new students anticipate these lessons the most.

A magic doll created for surveillance tasks to ensure the security of the castle. They walk around on two legs attached to an iron helmet and will faithfully alert their masters at once if they find an intruder. A simple, must-have doll wherever heightened security is required.

A red mushroom that lives in the World Tree Forest. They say Shirumi's cute appearance is a blessing from the World Tree itself. The round-tipped red hat is its greatest treasure. It still has some memories of when it was an ordinary mushroom, so when it is startled by a natural enemy, still emits a light in response.

A morph that was meant to be scary to ward off evil spirits, but it's too friendly-looking to be truly terrifying. This barely-spooky morph is a real festival crowd-pleaser. When a group of friends all gather together in this festive form, it's hard not to smile.

A mysterious goblin that walks around with a sack of gifts on its back when the festival starts. People were very suspicious at first, but when it was discovered that these gifts were actually for those who couldn't come to the festival, people named it the "Gift Goblin," and took to waiting for the goblin's visit with their own gifts prepared to donate.

Created by an eccentric Venelux wizard, this morph was originally meant to terrify even the bravest of foes. However, as soon as people discovered how fun it was to dance in, it became all the rage on the dance floor instead. Now the form is better known for being groovy than scary (much to the dismay of its creator).

The most popular magic doll in the toy shop. Children can't get enough of this furry bear humorously riding a unicycle. Even crying children will start to laugh out of joy when they see this doll. This doll is always displayed at the center of the shop due to its popularity.

Each spring, the Young Mage Academy in Venelux holds a Limong Festival that features various events. The main competitions include jumping and rolling races. Residents of the nearby village gather to watch these races, and they have become a central element of the festival.

The second basic morph learned after Oremong is the Giant Oremong Morph. A special spell must be added in order for the caster to grow in size. If you make one mistake at that juncture, you will not be able to return to your original shape for a few hours afterward and must simply live as an Oremong for that time.

Harvesters are simple dolls powered by magic that operate on their own. Magic academies have a tradition of presenting these dolls to students to give to their families. Rural areas use them to chase away pests and birds. However, the Harvesters of the Golden Rye Pastures have had their Magic Schema corrupted by the cursed rain and now attack anything on sight, unable to distinguish pests from humans.

A type of goblin from the Urstella clan that inhabits the Urstella Fields. They are very fond of the sparkling crystals found in Starcluster Flowers and are naturally hostile to humans who try to steal them. Wearing helmets and armor and wielding axes, they pose a threat to both merchants and adventurers alike if they try to touch the Starcluster Flower.

It is said that this orc that the God of Fire created is popular as a shapeshifting option, but it's purely preferential, and some people won't use it. But you will need an orc disguise one way or another if you want to enter the land of orcs.

Long ago, Skeleton soldiers appeared on the battlefield marched on and on, armed with weapons and armors stripped off from other fallen soldiers. These undying, victory-craving Skeletons became the frequent topic of nightmares.
An Orc Spearmaster from the Akidu clan. They are very vicious and expertly wield spears taller than themselves.

A lycan from the Kowazan clan that resides in the Grayclaw Forest. They appear human during the day, but they are abnormally violent and impulsive. They are very muscular and can easily wield a heavy mace that a regular human would struggle to lift.

These monstrous lobsters can mainly be found at Windhill Shores and have a similar shape and color as rocks commonly seen along the coast. They have low intelligence and live in groups. Upon encountering prey, they attack with their giant pincers. They are also able to fire powerful jets of water from a distance to stun their opponents.

Mitrans are one of the oldest species in this world. They originated from the first seed created by Einar, which was grown into a beautiful tree with the water of life. It is said that they are the fathers of all plant life and generally care after all life forms as a parent would.

Giant spiders that live in the Carmine Forest. Their bodies are dark green and their legs are black. They hide in bushes and pounce upon unwary travelers, knocking them to the ground with their two giant front legs before moving in for the kill.

The scarabs native to the Laslan Golden Rye Pastures mutated into giants after being exposed to the cursed rain. They retaliate fiercely when attacked and are covered with a hard shell. They charge their prey with their large horns, which are also valued for their medicinal properties. If you choose to morph into the form of a scarab, be careful not to run afoul of the local Harvesters created to destroy them!

Each orc clan has their own preferred diety which they dutifully honor with ceremonies and festivals. For instance, the Fonos clan serves Flamakan, the god of fire who they honor with their Festival of Fire. During these festivals, the Chief Priest and shamans use a fire ritual to empower their fellow clan members.

Though once human, only destructive instincts remain in a Skeleton, a fiend created by imbuing a burning rage into a dead person's bones. Once they are set upon a target, they swarm around them with weapons in hand, mindlessly and ceasingly raining blows until the target is annihilated. Although Skeleton Archers, which deal damage from a distance are a particularly feared menace, being shapeshifted into one can prove particularly helpful.
It is said that the Resistance in Laslan struggles with fighting these Skeleton Lancers because of their long and short ranged lance attacks.

Like other Undead, Skeletons are created through abuses of the Dark Power and its mastery over death. The formidable Skeleton Knights, which wield a mace in each hand, have left many a Resistance solider cowering in terror.

Ahzreil, the 6th Grand Elder of the Sylavean Order, lead an assault on the Lightbringer Society hiding in Laslan to exterminate them once and for all. But the Lightbringer wizards fought back bravely, pushing Ahzreil all the way back to the Shattered Temple, where he turned into a Specter. This was the start of the Eternal War.

Giants spiders that live in the Carmine Forest. When it gets dark, their bodies start to glow like lanterns. They hide on top of trees, then silently climb down to attack their prey. They can also shoot sticky webs from afar.

The most belligerent of the wolf varieties roaming the Blackhowl Plains. They sport bright, sand-colored fur and sharp fangs. Upon entering striking range, they dash toward their target and attack without mercy. Because they can run as fast as an arrow, they are also known as Arrow Wolves.

An extremely vicious wolf species that is native to the Blackhowl Plains. Covered from head to toe in white fur, these predators are very agile. When they spot their prey, they then leap high into the air and clamp their jaws around their targets' necks. While these creatures live in a pack, they prefer to hunt alone. However, when it comes to pack defense, they will not hesitate to work together as a team.

The most common wolf variety of the Blackhowl Plains. Their whole bodies are covered with black fur. Because they never back down from a fight, once they have selected their prey, they will pursue their target relentlessly until one of them falls. One must be especially careful of these wolves at night when they become especially hard to detect.

These wolves dwell in the Blackhowl Plains. Completely covered in gray fur, they have extremely sensitive noses. With their highly developed senses, these are the variety of wolf that travelers in the Blackhowl Plains are most wary of. When one spots their prey, they pounce high into the air come down clamping their strong jaws around their target's neck. These terrifying beasts are thought to be a hybrid of the Brutal Wolf and Blackhowl Wolf.

Zombies, corpses that roam without a soul, can be considered dead bodies reanimated using the elements of dead soil (which represents despair) and corrupted water (which represents laziness). In the end, these creatures, made by fusing despair and laziness, are filled with hostility and hunger for the living, and this is thought to be the underlying power source that allows zombies to move.

Sloth is one of the fundamental elements of darkness. This power is used to create Sluggish Zombies, whose hunger that cannot be sated, no matter how much they consume. As a result, not even the tiniest creature is left alive in their presence.
The Sand Basilisks living in the Manawastes are often considered the "hounds of the Demon King." Their spikes, honed by the wind and sands, are as sharp as swords.

Some of the people who lost their homes to Lord Fernan Barvo of Stonegard turned to thievery in order to survive. These gangs eventually coalesced into a single group, calling themselves the Sandflame Bandits. Even after Stonegard was liberated, they remained as bandits. Despite this, they have not forgotten their origins as craftsmen and the quality of their weapons is noteworthy.

Back before the Resistance existed, the only way to escape from the tyranny of a lord was to wander aimlessly or become a bandit. Without any formal military training or armaments, the serfs taught themselves to fight by randomly swinging with anything they could find. Even today, the brawlers of the Sandflame Bandits value their legacy of improvisation, thinking nothing of using torches, chair legs, or anything else they can find as a club.

As the Sandflame Bandits grew in wealth and power, it became essential for them to protect their treasure. But standing guard over the desert is not an easy task, and most Sentries prefer looting than guarding.

A strange type of Demonic Beast that lives in the Manawastes, also known as the Demon King's Eye. Unlike their hard outer skin, their eyeballs are fragile and commonly become bloodshot due to the dry air of the Wastelands. When shapeshifted into one, you can cross the Wastelands without fear of being attacked by other Evil Eyes.

These dangerous creatures live in the Manawastes. Of all known Demonic Beasts, these are said to be the closest to resembling a true demon. While they do have wings, they cannot fly up to high altitudes due to their heavy bodies. While shapeshifted into an Imp Lancer, you can move safely through The Raging Wilds, avoiding attacks from other Imps.

The first known Zombie Mutt was created the day the flourishing commercial city of Turayne was destroyed by the Shadowmancers of Sylaveth. All inhabitants of the prosperous village were drained of their life force and killed or turned into zombies by Adentus. And, sadly, their faithful dogs did not escape this fate. Even now as mindless zombies, these dogs will not attack their owners.

Undead were created through intermingling of Dark Power and the essence of death. Zombies, one of the main types of Undead, are beings whose souls have been removed, leaving behind only a ravenous, mindless monster. Even coming near Plague Zombies, which carry infectious disease, is something other creatures will want to avoid.

Some Large Lobsters have taken to hiding themselves in conch shells in much the same way their crab relatives have done for generations. These are known as Hermit Lobsters. Their bodies gradually grow until they fit tightly in their shells, to the point that casting off the shell becomes difficult. Because they believe that their hard shells will protect them, they will not hesitate to attack opponents stronger than them. Their flesh is often used as bait for wolves because it gives off a powerful stench.

There was a time when Stone Crabs were a famous delicacy at Windhill Shores. But after the cursed rain fell and they grew huge, they became less desirable meals. Not only due to their more vicious nature, but also due to their new pungent odor. Nowadays, their flesh is mainly used as animal feed or as bait by hunters.
The Orc Archers of Fonos Basin are nimble, strong, and have good eyes. They can pierce their target from afar with a single shot.
Orc Brawlers, armed with shields and blunt weapons, bravely protect Fonos Basin. When you run into these war veterans, be prepared for a fierce battle.

Giant spiders that live in the Carmine Forest. They have dark red bodies and are bigger and much more aggressive than other spiders in the forest. They are quite swift and attack their prey with their strong front legs and fangs.
Poisonous giant spiders living in the Carmine Forest. Their bodies are yellow with black patterns and their legs are black. They confuse their prey with fast movements, and spit poison at them.
A boar species that lives in the deep forests of Laslan. They are aggressive, greedy, and temperamental. Their keen sense of smell helps them to find their favorite food, mushrooms, from far away.

When Ahzreil, the 6th Grand Elder of the Sylavean Order, was cornered by the forces of the Lightbringer Society, he created skeleton soldiers to change the tide of battle. These Gallu Soldiers are still here, threatening the safety of unsuspecting travelers.
Gallu Archers, created by Ahzreil, the Grand Elder of the Sylavean Order, are amazing snipers. They aim at their targets with glowing red eyes.

Ravenous Zombies were created the day the flourishing commercial city of Turayne was destroyed by the Shadowmancers of Sylaveth. The inhabitants of the prosperous village who were killed by the Shadowmancers became different types of zombies depending on their base natures, such as greed, despair, or laziness. Greed is linked to the element of fire.

A type of goblin from the Urstella clan that inhabits the Urstella Fields. Goblin Strongarms wear helmets and armor and wield large hammers. A prominent characteristic of Goblin Strongarms is that they do not grow beards because they can get in the way while engaging in physical activity. Rumor has it that in the past, a famous Goblin Strongarm drowned because his beard got stuck while he was building a bridge across a river. They are hostile toward humans who try to steal Stardust.

A type of goblin from the Urstella clan that inhabits the Urstella Fields. Save for a minority that become shamans, goblins who are naturally weak generally take up the practice of stone throwing. Goblin Stone Throwers have good eyesight and unexpectedly strong shoulders, so they are able to hit moving targets in one shot, even from afar.

A type of goblin from the Urstella clan that inhabits the Urstella Fields. Goblin Butchers come to battle equipped with helmets, armor, and dual axes, and are noted for wearing their long hair up. They have a custom of tying their hair high on their heads, and rumor has it that the higher a Goblin Butcher ties their hair, the stronger they are. They are hostile toward humans who try to steal Stardust.

A wild insect species inhabiting the Golden Rye Pastures in Laslan that grew giant due to the cursed rain. When provoked, they shoot venom or attack opponents with strong jaws and saliva. When shapeshifted into a Wasp, you can move safely while avoiding the attacks of other Wasps.

Mitrans grow by absorbing water, so they are vulnerable to all kinds of contamination through water. Contaminated Mitrans rapidly grow weaker and weaker, either dying or going berserk after losing their sanity. When the bountiful plains of Laslan were contaminated by the Shadowmancers' attacks, many Mitrans met a tragic end.
Some of the Skeletons that Ahzreil summoned became Gallu Knights that wield dual swords. The red glowing eyes under their helmets are always looking for their next victims.

A type of goblin from the Urstella clan. Though Goblin Shamans are physically weak, they make up for it with a special form of sorcery passed down through the generations. They will attack any human who tries to steal their Stardust on sight. Despite the relatively low level of the magic they cast with their staves, they are surprisingly powerful.

A variety of huge boar that lives in the Carmine Forest. They are gray and have very stiff hairs on their backs. Their chins and tusks are extraordinarily strong. When they spy their prey, they quickly charge in.

When the Festival of Fire starts, the Chief Priest of the Fonos clan creates the Fire Shroud and puts orcs into a state of hallucination. Be careful, entering the Shroud without the protection of Fire Energy could kill you.

Feathered Terror Birds travel at high speeds and swoop at opponents with their razor-sharp talons. Their beaks are also sharp and hard enough to break rocks. These violent-tempered birds tend to leave their eggs exposed to external elements, just like other Terror Birds. This strange characteristic unique to this species invites attacks from natural enemies and keeps the population in check.

Headcrusher Terror Birds have thick skulls but decreased intelligence due to frequent headbutting. They sometimes forget who they were attacking as a result! However, their strong human-sized legs and terrifying beaks make them sufficiently fearsome opponents. It is essential to be shapeshifted into a Headcrusher Terror Bird when approaching the Nesting Grounds.

Sporting robust legs and bodies covered in red feathers, Thick-Billed Terror Birds stare down opponents with their sharp eyes and use their large, broad beaks to stun and bite them. They are also known as Hammerhead Terror Birds because of this ability to stun targets. They earned nother nickname, Hellbound Terror Bird, because they never let go until whatever poor creature they have locked inside their jaws is dead.

The Quillix, a mutated rodent, has spines all over their bodies. They are typically docile creatures that live in groups along the riverside, but are ferocious in combat situations. Those who have seen their fierce glare in such circumstances often refer to them as "piny Devil Rats."

A variety of lycan from the Kowazan clan that resides in the Grayclaw Forest. They appear human during the day, often wearing feathered cloaks to make them look bigger. Their eyesight is too keen and sensitive, so they often have to cover one of their eyes if they wish to move around during the day.
A variety of lycan from the Kowazan clan that resides in the Grayclaw Forest. They look human during the day, but they are very cruel in nature and kill any intruder they spot in the forest.
Orc Bowmen hail from the Akidu clan. They value their whale horn bow more than their own lives, and they never miss their prey.
Orc Executioners hail from the Akidu clan. These aggressive orcs can fight for three days straight without resting, and they use only half-covered helmets to show off their courage.
Orc Shadowmancers are from the Akidu clan. They wield magic staves with magical beasts' eyes to cast dark magic.

A variety of large scorpion that live in the Abandoned Stonemason Town. They are purple and have a bent tail with red poison sac on the tip. They always keep their tails up, so that they can attack enemies right away when they see one.

A variety of wolf from the Kowazan clan that reside in the Grayclaw Forest. They are very obedient to their masters. Lycans have a very keen sense of smell, and they can tell the difference between their wolves and imposters, so turning into a wolf won't help to pass by them.

The Temitrans of The Raging Wilds are a variation of Mitrans. People often mistake them for dried trees. They are quite docile during the day and won't attack passing travelers unless they are provoked.

The many Stone Golems roaming The Raging Wilds are the remnants of when a wizard brought stones to life to serve him in the past. Though these Stone Golems were created as weapons in the war against the Temitrans, they have since become a threat to humans. When shapeshifted into a Stone Golem, you can move among other Stone Golems without being threatened.

Some of the Stone Golems found in The Raging Wilds are made up of huge boulders. These powerful creations have a habit of summoning other Stone Golems, so extra caution is required when approaching one. When shapeshifted into a Large Stone Golem, you can safely move among other Stone Golems without being threatened.

The Desert Cobra of the Monolith Wastelands is famous for its colorful appearance. It is said that aristocrats of the desert raise Desert Cobras for ornamental purposes due to the light green spots covering their bodies and their thin wings that cover a wide area when unfurled. When shapeshifted into a Desert Cobra, you can safely move through the Monolith Wastelands without being attacked by other Desert Cobras.

The cobras inhabiting the Moonlight Desert possesses lethal venom. Their venom is potent enough to fell ten camels with a single drop. Their bodies, made up of numerous flexible joints, move as fast as lightning, even on sand. Even the heat of the scorching desert cannot stop the Lethal Venom Cobra.

A type of basilisk that lives in the Abandoned Stonemason Town. Usually, these creatures dig a huge maze-like underground nest and stay there. The scholar who first discovered the basilisk said in his notes that "this creature with a sharp horn, fangs, and a mace-like tail is indeed a nightmare given form in the real world."
Orc Butchers hail from the Akidu clan. They are very cruel and vicious, and they prefer to use clubs as to prolong their defeated enemies' agony.
Orc Fighters come from the Akidu clan. They use a special type of club forged in a smithy. They are especially hostile against members of the Resistance.

A variety of spider that lives in the Sandworm Lair and takes care of Sandworms' eggs and larvae. At night, they hold their legs up like a cage to protect themselves before they go to sleep. They are always on guard in their duty to protect the Sandworm eggs.
A type of symbiotic spider that lives in the Sandworm Lair. Their yellow and black patterns stand out among other spiders. They are very poisonous.

Your average Iron Chestacean of Daybreak Shore is very well aware of the importance of disguise. They use steel chests found on the beach as their houses, and as a bonus they can easily prey on travelers who rejoice at the sight of their newly found "treasure chests."

Sea crabs may look like slightly bigger versions of non lethal regular crabs, but their pincers are strong enough to cut a person in half. Their shells are extremely hard as well, offering a level of protection rivaling the best suits of plate armor.

Hermit Crabs are well known for their creepy human skull like body shape. Some travelers even avoid the Daybreak Shore, just so they won't run into these crabs. People will sometimes pick fights with these crabs as a test of courage.

The Armadillos inhabiting the Moonlight Desert grow to enormous proportions and are covered all over with hard scales. Though these Moonlight Scales are an expensive material used for high-end clothing and armor, hunting the fierce Armadillo recklessly will only get you torn to shreds by its sharp claws. While they usually travel slowly in groups, they are able to detect enemies very quickly.

The Sand Turtles inhabiting the Moonlight Desert are also called Backpack Turtles because of the shape of the shell on their back. They move slowly but are highly intelligent: they can hide by mimicking a rock in the sand, only to jump up and attack when prey draws near. They also have a powerful bite, making them a threat to any who cross the desert.
Mandrakes are strange looking plant creatures that stay half-buried in the ground. They attack their enemy with a shriek. A popular legend claims that anyone who hears this shriek will soon die.
A strange-looking type of plant creature that grows in the Abandoned Stonemason Town. They never have enough water, which makes their leaves red and poisonous.

Starlight Fireflies are a favorite species of Daybreak Shore on account of how they shine brightly in the dark, as if they were a cluster of stars. It is said that many adventurers who come to see this mysterious night spectacle are lured into the sea by their light. When shapeshifted into a Starlight Firefly, you can safely fly away from the dangerous monsters on Daybreak Shore.

A variety of scarab that lives in the Sandworm Lair and transports the sandworms' eggs and larvae. They are covered with spiky shells, and their sharp horns can lift things that are a dozen times heavier than themselves.

A unique variety of reptile inhabiting the Moonlight Desert. The name "Spineback Lizard" is derived from the threatening spike-like spines on their backs. Their strong jaws can crush human bones with a single bite. As such, these beasts are notorious among adventurers for their ferocity. If you encounter one of these in the desert, the best response is to run away.

The Bercant dominion was ravaged by Florification, a plant-based curse that originated from the mansion, cursing the populace with bizarre and even monstrous appearances. In the end, the residents lost their ability to reason and became monsters, hostile towards the humans who destroyed the forests. Florified Fruit humans were once hunters or herbalists who collected fruits in the forest. They have thorny vines wrapped around their bodies. When they encounter humans, they attack with sharp daggers.

A member of the ogre clan that lives in the Forest of the Great Tree. Despite their rough appearance, they like small and pretty things and often prey on the souls of elves attracted to the Great Sage Tree. This ogre gets so distracted by sparkling souls that they sometimes scratch or even lose their eyes to sharp branches, though that doesn't stop them. When Wolpertingers attempt to defend the wandering elven souls, this ogre swings huge clubs to keep them from getting closer.

One of the golems used in the Black Anvil Forge. This construct is exceptionally skilled with the tools attached to its hands, which can double as weapons in combat. Because it is an early model of golem, manufacturing is getting harder as replacement parts are scarce. However, because it is easy to operate, the golem is still widely used.

Explosive Marsharks that live in the Swamp of Silence have multiple explosive sacs on their large, round bodies. Since their eyes have completely degenerated, they rely on their sense of touch and keen hearing to hunt their prey. Since this makes precision attacks difficult, they instead charge in the general direction of their prey and cause explosions in hopes of damaging their targets.

About a thousand years ago, golems existed in Quietis's Demesne to protect the Temple of Truth. However, when Deluzhnoa appeared, powerful water magic covered the entire area. As the golems were powered by magic, they became dominated by the beast's rampage and developed a strong hostility toward humans. They now only listen to Deluzhnoa's orders and use water magic to punish enemies who invade their territory.

Numerous biological weapons were created in the Crimson Family's laboratory, using plants, animals, and humans alike as test subjects. The subjects that were successful were used in further testing, while those that failed were bred for observation or discarded. This subject, once an ill-fated guard dog, was turned into a feral, mutant monster. Lazarus freed the would-be guard dog the day before its scheduled disposal, allowing it to escape further testing and procreate. Now, these territorial mutants have spread beyond the manor's lab, still guarding their home.

The Black Anvil Dwarves, with their sturdy statures, have the strength to rival any other race, but are vulnerable to magical attacks and defenses due to their innate lack of magical power. To make up for these shortcomings, the great chieftain Pakilo Naru made a staff out of obsidian, the main mineral of the Black Anvil. Thus, the Black Anvil Dwarf Wizard was born, a foe that is both physically strong and skilled with magic. However, due to their short history of magic research, the types of magic that can be used are still limited.

Reville Lupius and Kazar Simosen, after occupying the Kingdom of Solisium, founded the Arkeum Legion to solidify their power. The Arkeum soldiers, with Kazar as their Chief Commander, were merciless enforcers. These troops were equipped with weapons and armor enchanted with black magic, making it seemingly impossible for anyone to oppose them. To this day, many still tremble with fear at the mere sight of their black armor.

The Crimson Family conducted cruel biological experiments in their underground laboratory, mercilessly sacrificing numerous animals in the process. Over time, the accumulated resentment created many vengeful wraiths. Among them, the Wraith Hound that roams the basement of the Crimson Mansion is well known for its vicious fangs, which it uses to tear into any intruders.

In the Year 1041, a delegation that was sent to Grasia from Solisium disappeared in the Nimogos Ocean. The royal wizards used all of their abilities to scan the nearby waters, but they found no trace of any wrecked ship. Among the lost was Kamarshea, a legendary knight of Solisium and the only daughter of the distinguished Marquis Kalten. She was a hero who saved many lives and earned a reputation for bravery by often putting her own life on the line from the very first minute she was made an apprentice knight. She was beloved as the guardian of the weak, and news of her disappearance cast a dark shadow over Solisium Castle.

Eldrin was a forest clan that worshiped nature and aimed to form a peaceful civilization. Legends say they were born of the World Tree in a time long past. Elowen was daughter of the Mirror Lake Forest Chieftain. When she was young and full of curiosity, she ventured beyond the outskirts of her forest and saw humans slaughtering elves. She was appalled by their cruelty and developed a fear of humans. Afterwards, she committed herself to harsh training in use of the sword and bow in order to be able to protect the forest from any invasion.

The decline of the Akidu clan began with the death of the first chieftain and lasted a long time. Then, on a night marked by the rise of a red moon, a hero was born in a place deep within the canyon—the hero who would lead the revival of the Akidu clan. Valkarg was known as the Beast because of the overwhelming strength he possessed since childhood that enabled him to tear apart enemies in battle with just his bare hands. He is driven by an insatiable desire to attain even greater strength.

Lord Mason of the Trutizan Mountains fought bravely against the Arkeum's invasion, but he was ultimately defeated, suffering severe injuries in the process. Enraged, Kazar ordered his forces to find and kill Lord Mason and his entire family. Only his young daughter Stheno managed to escape. She and several of her father's faithful servants made their way into the Eldrin Forest. Unfortunately, they were all hunted down by the forest-dwelling Eldrin clan, who despised humans on principle. Stheno alone was spared by Elowen, the guard captain of the forest. Stheno managed to make her way to a road, but ultimately fainted from starvation where she was found by a shaman named Marcos from the Sylavean Order.

As an unmatched assassin, it was his first failure, and that failure turned into a massacre. When he awakened, everyone else around him was dead. But was he alive? He instinctively and immediately knew that he had been transformed into a completely different being. Having lost everything dear to him—his comrades, his life, his love—he was granted a new, immortal life after death. It wasn't long until he realized how he should use it.

After being bitten by a vampire, Ezekiel was saved by Scarla, a monster hunter. He survived with Scarla's help but had become a half-vampire in the process. In despair, Ezekiel attempted to commit suicide, but Scarla suggested that he became a vampire slayer to help save people from the fate he almost succumbed to. Ezekiel agreed and started to train by learning various martial disciplines from Scarla. Ezekiel developed a deep sense of gratitude to her for giving him a new lease on life.

Gregory, a wizard of Trutizan who specialized in research on Diabolica, learned to communicate with a demon named Dantalux while studying an ancient mask. Dantalux's voice from the mask suggested that they play an enticing game involving betting on the forbidden knowledge of demons and a human soul. Dantalux used Gregory's foolishness and human greed to eventually take over his body.

Once a great noble's jester, Charlie escaped to a forgotten room in the castle's basement when he was beaten by his master after he returned in defeat from a battle. After finding a portrait of a knight covered by a dusty cloth (perhaps the noble's ancestor), Charlie mocked the figure by pretending to be a knight, but was shocked out of his mind once he heard a sound coming from the portrait. When the portrait promised to make him into a great knight if Charlie shared his blood with the figure, Charlie smeared his blood on the portrait, and came to possess both the appearance and power of the knight.

Pluton was once a low-ranking knight of a humble family. However, the king he served saw his skills and loyalty and held him in high esteem. Each time he achieved a meritorious deed, he was promoted and rewarded generously. And in return, Pluton pledged even higher and deeper loyalty. He became the king's most outstanding knight, and his shield.

It seemed as if the entire world gave their blessing to the birth of the daughter of the Elf King, Erendriel. She was always vibrant and energetic, as she had everything she could possibly need or want while growing up. Her older sister, Rafadriel, especially loved and adored her. Erendriel looked up to her older sister so much that she insisted on training in archery to be like her. It was the king's wish for her not to train in weapons, but he lost the argument as she convinced him that she'll need it for self-defense. While her older sister would stick with the longbow, Erendriel wound up favoring crossbows.

The elf king, Lindriel, was troubled over the fact that he and his wife were unable to bear children. Thus, during the war, he decided to adopt a baby girl whose father had died in a battle. The king named the baby Rafadriel. Baby Rafadriel grew up to be a healthy girl and showed a talent in archery. Those who disliked her would taunt her over the fact that she was adopted. None of this fazed her. Rather, she became more resolute to become a better daughter and worked tirelessly to prove herself worthy of her royal titles.

When the seeds of conflict between Elves and Humans began to sprout, two quiet children were born in a field covered in white snow. The twins were half-elves born of a elven mother and a human father, and could never learn how to speak. However, as the relations between Humans and Elves worsened, the twin's parents had no choice but to separate. The older sister, Taliesia, followed her mother and settled in elven society. However, due to her mixed blood, Taliesia was always treated as an outcast among elves, and when her mother passed away from a sudden sickness, Taliesia became a loner neglected by society.

Dreadal lived with his mother in Tersia Forest, far away form the village. When his mother's sickness worsened and she was not able to move easily, Dreadal soon became the breadwinner. He gathered herbs from the forest and hunted small animals to sell at the village. His mother told Dreadal to always disguise himself before going to the village. Although he couldn't understand why at first, as he grew up, he realized that he was different from others. When Dreadal came of age, his mother told him that he was the descendant of the Elves, and that she raised him after finding him abandoned. After learning of his origin, Dreadal held his mother tight, thanking her for raising him so well. In his embrace, her mother quietly passed away.

Behemog was a leading contender to become the next chieftain of the Fonos Clan. He was set apart by his unmatched strength and charisma, and his rare wisdom—unusual for an orc—and quick wit rivaling that of humans earned him both the admiration and envy from his peers. Though gifted in many ways, what truly made him stand out was his fiery passion for love that even the shaman Flamakan failed to quell. In the entire history of the Fonos Orcs, there was never another philanderer like Behemog.

Once the most radiant beauty in the land, Velina's grace became a curse when she fell victim to the vile desires of a greedy lord's son and his followers. When her brother dared protest, they beat him half to death. Paralyzed by fear, their parents urged silence, telling her to obey and survive. Consumed by rage and despair, Velina fled to an abandoned chapel. There, she cursed the gods and prepared to end her own life. But just then, she heard a voice echoing through the darkness: "I will become your blade. Give me their souls."

As a child, Vechere survived the massacre of her village during the war and was fleeing for her life when she was discovered by a reclusive human wizard living in a remote tower. The wizard offered to take her in, promising that if she became his apprentice and assisted with his magical research, he would one day help her take revenge. Grateful for her rescue, young Vechere eagerly accepted his offer and began learning about the magical artifact he was studying: the Magic Orb.

Aranka was the strongest and most violent warrior among the numerous orcs of the Fonos Clan. Her cruelty bordering on madness made no distinction between friends or foe. All her opponents, whether they be elders or warriors in their prime, all met the same fate. In the end, Chief Fonos prepared a separate place just for her. He released her onto the battlefield where she could slaughter indiscriminately.

An intruder has appeared in the World Tree's forest. The vicious lord Kumalon brought his soldiers and set fire to take over the land for himself. The Jade Rock Clan sacrificed their lives to fight against the lord's army, but it was not enough to stop the invaders and their fires. However, an order of brave knights came to their aid. Although they were humans, they drove out the enemy ravaging the forest and stood by Eldrin's side.

An adorable, happy-go-lucky dog. Its abundant fur is as soft as silk, but the static is so strong that even a gentle breeze makes the air thrum with electric current. This canine once hid in a deep, secluded valley until a kindly wizard took the lonely beast. They built Pompom a sturdy but transparent orb that negated its electric currents. Now that it won't accidentally shock anyone, Pompom clearly loves its new home, eager to roll its ball around and meet as many people as it can.

Originally from the grasslands of Trutizan, Almirazes can now be found in many areas of Solisium. Given their cute rabbit-like appearance, some people are shocked to learn that they are classified as predators, as they have a ferocious nature and will attack anyone they don't like with their horns. Larger versions of the species have various elemental characteristics, similar to elemental spirits, which can be seen in the color of their fur.

Raccoons were first discovered in the dense woods in northern Solisium. While they're most well-known for washing their food, their sneaky and extremely timid nature makes this trait difficult to observe. They usually reside in hollow logs or tunnels, and they threaten enemies by standing on their hind legs to make themselves look bigger. Raccoons are also actually curious and sociable; they sometimes even wear human clothing and accesories, which were offered as tokens of friendship.

The alpaca is believed to have originated from an arid island southeast of Solisium. They boast lustrous, shimmering fleece and seem to enjoy carrying loads on their backs. Alpacas primarily feed on cacti, and their gentle nature makes them well-suited for domestication.

First discovered in the northern undersea canyons of Trutizan, the Kelpi has a sleek body and wing-shaped fins. Its body is dark-hued, but the fin running from head to tail glimmers with vivid colors. Though it dwells in the deep sea, folklore says it surfaces during great storms, shrouding the waters in heavy mist as a warning.

The Ray was first discovered in the waters off Nimogos. This fantastical creature has a broad, flattened body that glows brighter the darker its surroundings. It has been spotted leaping to the surface in the middle of the night in distant waters. Its mysterious glow has led many to dive into the sea, earning it the nickname "Devil of the Night."

The Drakan is a small to medium ocean-dwelling dragonkin that effortlessly roams the oceans. Its streamlined body, webbed limbs, and elegant dorsal fins, allow for agile navigation through the seas, while an elongated, flexible neck grants lethal precision when hunting. The vibrant fins along its back not only enhance propulsion but also serve to intimidate rivals or impress potential mates with a majestic display.

The Gryphon is a Mystic Beast with four clawed legs and big, strong wings that lives in the rugged highlands of Talandre. Legend has it that it's the gatekeeper of the expanse, the towering mountains at the command of the wind god, Ventius. With its wings outstretched, the Gryphon lives up to its reputation, overwhelming onlookers with its majesty.

Vapulon is a mythical beast dwelling in the harsh ravines of the frigid climate. It boasts a powerful physique, a magnificent mane, and vast wings. Revered for its mysterious majestic form, ancient legends describe it as a divine messenger who delivers wisdom and craftsmanship from the gods. It is said that Vapulon's roar commands every creature of the heavens and the earth.

Squirrels are flying creatures of the rodent family, gliding gracefully through forests and villages. Known for their close bond with humans, they possess remarkable memory and keen observation skills. These playful companions often bring small gifts or perform tricks for those they trust. It is said they bring joy and fortune to the households they live with. Their fondness for wearing tiny clothes or ornaments given by humans makes them resemble whimsical little fairies, earning them the love of many.

Glasha is a fox with brightly colored butterfly wings, fluttering with the light, sprightly grace of a fairy. It dwells mostly in deep forests, feeding on small insects and tree fruits. Known for its curiosity and gentle nature, it is said that the ancient elves once kept Glasha as a pet.

The Big Tidebully Goblin isn't just here to swim, he's here to be seen. Even when enjoying a simple day at the beach, this peacocking patriarch insists on bold fashion accessories to garner attention. His tube and beach ball, as alluring as they are, are rare items that are nearly impossible to find.

A goblin that loves the sea so much it never leaves the beach. When the heatwaves peak, it shows up with a cute little inflatable tube and a massive beach ball, turning the coastline into its own water playground.

A morph spell created by a mischievous professor at Venelux, inspired by the many expressions he often saw on his students' faces. It's said these were the looks they gave when called on to answer a question - or when he suddenly appeared before someone who had broken the rules. Though a bit impish, the comical form of the Oremong reflects the professor's fondness for his students.

Llamas are herbivorous animals that mainly inhabit temperate highlands and grasslands. Though generally gentle, they may spit as a defensive response when feeling threatened. Llamas live in herds and can be domesticated. They are well-suited for carrying loads, making them a key type of livestock in Talandre. While their comical braying and perpetually unimpressed expression often lull travelers into lowering their guard, they may flee abruptly or erupt in a tantrum if frightened.

A prolific, sleep-deprived wizard raising eight children unwittingly invented a transformation spell. That day, after his youngest "researched" pancake ingredients onto the floor, his third child sobbed over a "fashion crisis," and his eldest summoned elemental spirits past bedtime, the exhausted parent snapped—morphing into a grotesque Oremong to stomp after the giggling horde of children. The children adored this impromptu game of tag. The neighbors, rudely awakened by roars of "BED! NOW!", could only look on in sympathy, eyes brimming with tears for the wizard.

In one corner of the Venelux Junior Magic School was a small orchard filled with luscious fruits. Mischievous students would often morph into Oremongs and hide among the branches to surprise passing workers. Most of them fled in a hurry, but those who didn't escape ended up lined up along the orchard wall, wearing sheepish smiles as they took their punishment. Their professor later sealed their mischievous forms in a Morph magic and presented it as a graduation gift.

Driven by curiosity, a Venelux professor once morphed into an Oremong to secretly attend a student party, hoping to understand them better. But the trending jokes and slang completely baffled them, and in frustration, they rolled on the floor in despair. The students quickly saw through this suspicious Oremong but kindly played along. Later, they devised an Oremong Morph magic capturing the professor's exact expression, honoring their effort and warm heart for years to come.

One mischievous student at Venelux devised a Morph spell just to tease his friends. Countless students fell victim to his tricks, but his proudest moment was startling a boy who had come to deliver a gift and letter to the girl he liked. The boy fainted on the spot, and the prankster never revealed his identity. At least the school gained another spooky rumor out of it.

An unknown sculptor carved a Gigantrite pumpkin to capture its majestic form and commemorate the Haunted Harvest. Eager to preserve his masterpiece forever, the sculptor even commissioned a wizard to create a Morph spell for it. Unfortunately, he couldn't break the spell himself and was forced to remain in pumpkin form throughout the entire festival.

A farmer carved Whisperion, the World Tree of Whisp Island, into a big, juicy pumpkin to make a stunning pumpkin lantern. So many people wanted one that a benevolent wizard used morph magic to make more. Since then, rows of World Tree pumpkin lanterns have often been seen decorating town squares during the Haunted Harvest.

A pumpkin lantern carved with the likeness of the infamous Witch of Chaos, whose name spread across all of Solisium. Though she merely vanished in the turmoil of war, people carved her image into lanterns of the dead, praying she would never return. Some even enchanted these lanterns into Morphs, believing that her overwhelming power would ward off Specters.

At the Venelux Youth School of Magic, a grand party is held every year at the end of the term to celebrate the students' advancement. The dining hall joins the festivities by creating a large, ornate cake to honor them. One year, a tangy-sweet cake brimming with fresh Oremong became the highlight of the event. One student, having forgotten they were in Morph form as an Oremong, happily enjoyed the cake. The blissful expression on their face brought laughter to everyone, inspiring the creation of a morph spell modeled after that moment.

One unusually refreshing morning, a drowsy Oremong stirred just before realizing they had overslept. Maybe it was because they had fallen asleep in Oremong form after practicing Morph magic all night. In any case, if they start rolling now, they just might barely make it on time.

One brave student at the School of Magic once ventured into an empty classroom in the dead of night to secretly share his feelings for the girl he liked. Afraid of being discovered, he even transformed into an Oremong, placed a gift and letter on her seat, and turned away with a satisfied smile. But just then, something huge and round burst out of the darkness toward him! Shocked beyond belief, the boy fainted on the spot, and the Oremong's terrified expression was forever sealed in a Morph spell—becoming "proof" of one of the school's ghost stories.

A loyal Pumpkin Hound guarding the Haunted Labyrinth. Fed daily on the finest gourds by the Pumpkin King, it cannot be bribed with any delicacy. Yet throw a small pumpkin, and it will joyfully chase after it, earning the affection of adventurers despite its duty as a sentry.

The Golden Goblin Chief, a goblin of high standing among his kin. He holds enormous sway over Thief Goblins and is rumored to have amassed an incredible fortune. Many adventurers scour the land in search of him and his treasure, yet the only ones they ever catch are other adventurers morphed into the Goblin Chief. Because of this, some frustrated treasure hunters end up hitting adventurers instead of the real Goblin Chief.

A Golden Goblin with a black hat pressed down low, always scheming for a chance to claim the Golden Goblin Chief's seat. Adventurers who've been chased after morphing into a Golden Goblin Chief often try morphing into a Black Hat Golden Goblin as a backup, but they say people chase them away just the same.

According to the legend of the Startree Solstice, the Snowman Fairy was created when a wizard enchanted a decorated snowman to help the Gift Grandmother, who was busy baking cookies. Children's eyes light up in anticipation of gifts when a Snowman Fairy appears.
A prismatic multicolored Oremong created by an eccentric wizard from Venelux. Bored with Oremong Morph classes in school, they mixed various colors to create their own Oremong.

On days when snow falls softly, Snowbally appears from nowhere to deliver gifts before departing. Each beautifully wrapped chest is filled with blessings, and it's said that the kinder and more honest the person, the heavier their chest will be.
You are treated as the same tribe as this entity.

Designed to swiftly detect and respond to intruders at base fortresses. Though small in stature, they possess great strength and nimble movement, making them especially suited to standing guard alone in narrow passageways. According to the soldiers who served alongside them, seeing their long spears get tangled together and spin around on the way back from a mission is quite adorable.
